question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Imagine your guests getting check-in details, check out times, Wi-Fi info, and answers to common questions automatically, 24/7. It saves you time, keeps your replies consistent, and gives your guests a smooth, professional experience, all without you lifting a finger. This is exactly what we're going to build together today, an Airbnb auto-reply WhatsApp chatbot using only WhatsBolt, no official WhatsApp API needed. Once we've linked our WhatsApp account, we can create our chatbot by selecting the WA chatbot option. Now, let's select the profile where we want to set up the chatbot and click on add item. I've created a document with all the keywords and their respective answers for our Airbnb chatbot, covering details like check-in, check-out, Wi-Fi, and more. We'll keep the status enabled. For not matching default response, choose yes. Then, set recipient type to individual, since we don't want this chatbot replying in group conversations. For type, it doesn't matter in this case because this will be our default response. Give your chatbot a name and a short description. Keywords aren't important in this step, so you can just type any keyword. For presence delay, set it to 3 seconds and enable show typing. This makes it feel like a real person is responding. Now, let's set the message a user will receive if their message doesn't match any keyword. In our case, this will act like an index message, listing all the keywords the user can send to interact with our chatbot. As you can see, our message includes all the keywords we want our chatbot to recognize and respond to. And with that, we've completed the first step of our chatbot. Just click submit and our default response is ready. Now, let's create a new item so we can start automating each keyword one by one. This message will handle check-in information. We'll set no match response to no and select individual as the recipient type. Then, we'll add the relevant keywords, in this case, check-in, along with the message the user will receive. Next, we'll add two more items, one for check out information and another for Wi-Fi information. For the Wi-Fi item, we'll also include the keyword internet so the chatbot can respond even if the user types that instead. Now, click the run button to activate the chatbot, and that's it. Our chatbot is now live and successfully sending automatic replies to our users.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Earlier this year, Insta 360 introduced the latest X5 action camera and later followed with the X5 Satin white limited edition variant, which we reviewed last month. Now, the action camera manufacturer Insta 360 has launched a new 360° action camera in its X series, the Insta 360 X4 Air. The company has advertised the X4 Air as the lightest ever, 8K 360° action camera in the brand's roster. Dimension-wise, it measures 46 x 113.8 x 37 mm, 1.81 x 4.48 x 1.45 in, and weighs just 165 g, 0.36 lbs, which is almost equal to the smartphone's weight. By contrast, the original X4 has the same dimensions, but it's slightly heavier than the X4 Air, weighing in at 203 g, 0.44 lbs. Insta 360 has incorporated dual 1/1.8-inch CMOS sensors into the X4 Air, which further helps to capture footage with better detail and more vivid colors. Like the X5, the action camera also ships with Insta 360's intelligent exposure algorithm, adaptive tone. Speaking of imaging capabilities, the CMOS sensor outputs at 29 megapixels with an F 1.95 aperture and a 6.4 mm equivalent focal length. It can capture 360° videos at up to 8K 30 FPS. Despite boasting a compact form factor, Insta 360 has managed to squeeze in a 2010 mAh battery into the X4 Air, and the brand claims that it offers up to 100 minutes of runtime when recording footage at 6K 24 FPS. While shooting at 8K 30 FPS, users can expect a runtime of around 88 minutes. Interestingly, like the X5, the latest X4 Air also supports user-replaceable lenses. On the positive side, it does offer all video modes from the flagship X5 action camera, including 360° video, active HDR, Instaframe mode, time-lapse, loop recording, road mode, and more. Furthermore, it's equipped with Insta 360's flow state stabilization and 360° horizon lock, which handles image stabilization related things. Users can easily auto-edit 360° footage, export videos, and edit images via the Insta 360 app. Unlike the X4, the Insta 360 X4 Air is compatible with most X5 accessories. Moreover, the action camera is rated at 49 ft, 15 m, and supports gesture controls.

answer: The story of American politics is a journey that begins in 1789 when George Washington took the oath as the first president of the United States. Since then, the presidency has shaped not only America, but the world. From Thomas Jefferson, who expanded the nation through the Louisiana purchase, to Abraham Lincoln, who held the Union together during the Civil War and ended slavery, the presidency became a test of leadership in the toughest of times. In the 20th century, Franklin D. Roosevelt led America through the Great Depression and World War II. John F. Kennedy inspired a generation with his call to ask not what your country can do for you. Each president left a mark that defined an era. Some presidencies brought scandal, like Richard Nixon's Watergate. Others, like Ronald Reagan's, reshaped American politics for decades. In 2008, Barack Obama made history as the nation's first African-American president, proving that the story of America is always evolving. Today, the presidency continues to be the most powerful office in the world, a position that reflects America's struggles, dreams, and its constant fight to live up to its ideals. The history of American presidents is not just about politics, it's about the story of a nation.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: SpaceX's Starship makes a dramatic splash. Witness the incredible video of the charred spacecraft's landing in the Indian Ocean after a triumphant flight test 11. This week's launch showcased the mighty Starship's final moments before its ocean landing, leaving spectators in awe. On October 13th, the 397-foot tall, 121-meter tall rocket embarked on its 11th test flight from SpaceX's Starbase in South Texas. This marked the last journey for the current Super Heavy booster and ship upper stage configuration, as a taller version is set to debut on the upcoming Starship flight 12. Flight test 11 exceeded expectations, outperforming its predecessor from the 10th flight. SpaceX released stunning footage revealing the spacecraft's resilience, showcasing minimal damage and discoloration compared to the previous flight. The mission achieved all objectives, from launch to booster descent and splashdown in the Gulf, and the ship's graceful landing in the Indian Ocean. This success marks the second consecutive test flight where Starship met all SpaceX's goals, a significant milestone in its development. But here's where it gets interesting. The spacecraft deployed eight simulated Starlink satellites and executed a Raptor engine relight in space. However, this flight diverged from flight 10's profile with modified engine burn patterns, a crucial step towards the rocket's upgraded version 3. The final descent was a spectacle with the upper stage's landing burn differing from previous flights. This time, it emulated the maneuver required for a return to the launch site, where the rocket's tower is designed to capture Starship mid-air during landing. SpaceX's drone and buoy cameras captured the breathtaking descent through the clouds, showcasing the unique flip and burn maneuver that gracefully positioned the spacecraft upright for landing. And this is the part that has space enthusiasts buzzing. The Starship's development is a testament to SpaceX's innovation, pushing the boundaries of what's possible in space exploration. But with great power comes great responsibility. As SpaceX continues to refine its technology, the question arises, how will these advancements impact the future of space travel and exploration? Will they revolutionize space tourism or lead to new scientific discoveries? The possibilities are endless and the debate is sure to spark passionate discussions. Stay tuned for more space adventures and don't forget to share your thoughts in the comments below.

In Seoul's Myeong-dong, a district crowded with foreign tourists, anti-China protests openly expressing hostility toward China have become serious. As damage to merchants and tourists grew, Prime Minister Kim Min-suk, following President Lee Jae-myung, also called for strong measures. Reporter Choi Ha-yon went on-site to show how serious it is.
People gathered on the street are tearing apart China's national flag, the Five-star Red Flag.
Chinese Communist Party out! Chinese Communist Party out!

Local merchants are trying to make a living by selling to tourists, but they completely wreck things like this.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: In a dramatic turn of events, billionaire Elon Musk has once again set the internet on fire. This time, by lashing out at a top Trump administration official over a lost government contract. The controversy began when Sean Duffy, the acting administrator of NASA and US Transportation Secretary, claimed that SpaceX, Elon Musk's company, is falling behind on its mission to return humans to the moon. Duffy even hinted that the US government might open the contract to other companies, sparking instant fury from Musk. Within hours, Musk took to his platform, X, formerly Twitter, and launched a series of posts mocking Duffy. He called him Sean Dummy, questioned whether someone with a two-digit IQ should be running America's space program, and then shared a meme with the caption, Why are you gay? That single post went viral instantly, not for humor, but for outrage. Critics accused Musk of being disrespectful, unprofessional, and even homophobic, saying such remarks cross the line for a public figure leading major government projects. Supporters, however, argue that Musk is simply fighting back against unfair government pressure and political bias. They point out that SpaceX has already revolutionized space travel and saved NASA billions through reusable rockets. But the timing couldn't be worse. The US government is reviewing its next phase of moon mission contracts, and Musk's public outburst may further strain his relationship with officials. What began as a corporate disagreement has now become a very public feud, blending politics, ego, and the high stakes of America's space ambitions. Whether Musk's bold defiance helps him or hurts him, only time will tell. But one thing's for sure, when Elon Musk speaks, the world listens, even if it's for all the wrong reasons.

At the India AI Impact Summit in Delhi, it wasn't just artificial intelligence in the air, it was the aroma of Araku and Kurk. I know I'm going to try the Malabar Arabica. I think that's close to. Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai took a break from high-level AI deliberations to sip Bharat GI coffee at a special lounge set up by Department of Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade of India. 
For a moment, the AI Summit turned into a celebration of India's soft power. GI tag, UPI innovation and cutting-edge AI, all blending seamlessly. But the real buzz came earlier in the day at Bharat Mandapam. Pichai went back in time, recalling his student days travelling on the Coromandel Express from Chennai to IIT Kharagpur. He spoke about a quieter Visakhapatnam, a city he remembers as brimming with potential. Every time I visit, I'm struck by the pace of change and today is no different. Back when I was a student, I often took the Coromandel Express train from Chennai up to IIT Kharagpur. To get there, we passed through Visakhapatnam, Vizag. I remember it being a quiet and modest coastal city, brimming with potential. Fast forward to 2026, and that potential just got turbocharged. Google is now setting up a full stack AI hub in Visakhapatnam as part of a massive $15 billion infrastructure investment in India. The hub will feature gigawatt scale compute capacity and a new international subsea cable gateway, effectively turning the coastal city into a global AI node. From train journeys to tech journeys, from IIT lecture halls to global boardrooms. From filter coffee to full stack compute, in one visit, Sundar Pichai blended heritage with high technology, underscoring India's growing identity not just as a market but as a produc- nation. And if this summit proved anything, it's that the future of AI might be brewed, coded and powered in India. Bureau Report, NDTV.

The time has come to review the UN regional architecture, to ensure it remains connected to the members that need it most. Solomon Islands remains underrepresented within the UN staff establishment. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Today's video is all about how to use a breast pump correctly in a simple and comfortable way. Many new moms feel confused when they start pumping, so this guide will help you understand each step clearly. Using a breast pump is completely natural and extremely helpful for mothers who want to store milk for their baby or maintain their feeding routine. Start by checking all the parts of your pump to make sure everything is clean and ready. Before placing the pump, sit in a comfortable position so the process goes smoothly. Gently place the breast shield on your skin, making sure it sits in the center and fits properly. Before turning on the pump, take a deep breath and relax because pumping works best when your body is calm. Turn on the pump and begin with the lowest suction setting. Slowly increase the suction until you find the level that feels comfortable for you. It may take a little time for the milk to start flowing, and that is completely normal. If you want, you can look at your baby's picture or use a warm compress to help trigger your let down reflex faster. Once the milk starts collecting in the bottle, let the pump run naturally. A session usually lasts around 10 to 15 minutes, but you can continue longer if your body needs more time. When you are done, switch off the pump and gently remove the shield. Transfer the milk into a safe storage container and place it in the refrigerator or freezer right away. Don't forget to wash all the pump parts with warm water and mild soap. Keeping everything clean is very important for your baby's health. Breast pumping is a simple routine that becomes easier with practice. Stay consistent and you'll feel more confident every day. I hope this tutorial helps you. If you enjoyed the video, make sure to like and subscribe for more helpful content.

Legacy, disruption, and the fight for control in a world shaped by technology. From the neon-lit skyline to the quiet hills above Tokyo, Japan offered the right tone, scale, and contrast to ground our narrative and gameplay. For fans in Japan, it's a chance to see their world reimagined through the lens of Black Ops. For players everywhere else, it's an invitation to explore one of the most visually and culturally rich settings we've ever built. Every detail was considered. Every space was designed to honor the setting while delivering the gameplay Black Ops is known for. This map's really exciting because we wanted to transport players into the player fantasy of being at the heart of Tokyo. For me as an objective player, I really love this map because it's got really well-defined lanes and then some really fun set pieces. One of my favorite things in the map is the cat cafe. There's a karaoke bar which is a lot of fun. Those as call outs where it's like, I got them in the cat cafe. That's going to be fun to say no matter what. Each of the landmarking across it is really unique from the old town district into the main center urban district where you're surrounded by this 2035 atmosphere, and then the carnage that spills from that as well. From the outside, you'll see this Japanese castle, and then once you make your way inside, the guild have taken it over and instilled this 2035 tech. I really love the throne room. It's in the center of this castle and it's got this amazing blend of technology. My favorite thing in this map are the wall jump opportunities on the outside lanes. You're going over the rooftop wall, other players are on the inside experiencing a completely different close quarters dynamic. On behalf of all of us at Treyarch, we are so excited for players to experience our new multiplayer maps during our upcoming beta starting next week. answer: Those displaced by floods are still fighting for their survival. The relief efforts are inadequate and the regency was not capable of handling this flood and landslide disaster alone. Though more than 1 million people have been displaced, the Indonesian government has so far ignored calls for a state of national disaster to be declared. Those demanding it say the measure would free up resources and improve the coordination of aid. Meanwhile, the government insists that crisis management is done by the provinces and that the 30 million US dollars in emergency funds should be enough, while also promising additional funding if needed. Indonesia has only declared a state of national disaster three times. First, during the 1992 earthquake, then in 2004 when a tsunami killed over 160,000 people, and finally during the COVID-19 pandemic. Some analysts are saying that the government is refusing to do so again to avoid any perception that it can't handle the crisis.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: From album of the year to the biggest stage in sports, Bad Bunny just turned the Super Bowl halftime show into a full-on celebration of Puerto Rico. But one detail from his outfit has fans talking, the number 64 stitched onto his jersey. So what does it mean? The show featured surprise appearances from Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin and transformed the field into a vibrant tribute to Puerto Rican culture. Style-wise, the details were just as intentional. He wore an Audemars Piguet watch, a Marquis diamond stud earring by Marvin Douglas, designed to echo the shape of a football, and a custom white football jersey by Zara. The jersey featured the name Ocasio, a nod to his real name Benito Antonio Martinez Ocasio. And now there's more clarity around the number 64 stitched across his chest. According to Complex, Bad Bunny was paying tribute to his late uncle, who previously played football and wore the same number. Before that detail emerged, fans had floated several theories. Some believed the number referenced his mother's birth year. Others connected it to the initial, widely criticized death toll reported after Hurricane Maria devastated Puerto Rico in 2017. There were even historical interpretations, including a nod to the 64th United States Congress, which passed the Jones-Shafroth Act granting U.S. citizenship to Puerto Ricans in 1917. Some pointed to 2023 when Bad Bunny's Un Verano Sin Ti became the first Spanish language album ever nominated for Album of the Year at the 64th Grammy Awards. At the 2026 Grammys, he made history again, winning Album of the Year for De Mi Tirar Mas Fotos, the first Spanish-language album to ever take home the top prize. That same night, he also turned heads on the red carpet in Schiaparelli's first-ever menswear design, and used his acceptance speech to protest ICE, declaring, we are humans and we are Americans. Those moments echoed into the halftime show, where he appeared to symbolically present his Grammy to a child watching his speech on a small TV, a powerful visual about legacy and representation. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell later praised the artist, saying Bad Bunny understood the weight of the platform and its power to unite people. Ahead of the game, an emotional Bad Bunny said the performance was about joy, culture, and heart, and dedicated it to those who came before him. With this latest confirmation, the meaning appears deeply personal, a family tribute layered into a performance already packed with cultural pride, history, and legacy.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to record a Google Slides presentation with both audio and video. Whether you opt to use the built-in recording feature in Google Slides or prefer to work with a versatile screen recording tool like Screencastify or Loom, I'll guide you through the process step-by-step to ensure you can effectively capture your presentation. Let's start by exploring Google Slides built-in recording feature. First, head over to slides.google.com and open the presentation you want to record. Once you're all set with your slides, look towards the top right corner of the interface. You'll notice a record button, easily identifiable by its circle within a circle icon. Click on this to move into the recording options. Upon clicking, select record new video to prepare for capturing your presentation. Now you can click the red record button, signaling the start of your recording session. At any time, should you need a break or wish to restart from a particular point, you're in control. You can pause and re-record as needed. Once satisfied, you can stop the recording and save it directly to your Google Drive for easy access and sharing. While setting up, manage your camera and microphone settings. Decide if you want them on or off, adjusting the picture and picture to your desired size and position on the screen for a personalized touch. Next, let's shift our focus to using an external screen recording tool. If you're opting for this, you'll start by choosing a tool such as Screencastify or Loom. These tools are great if you want more flexibility and functionality. After selecting your tool, set up your recording area. Choose either the full screen or a specific window that's most relevant to your presentation. Double check to make sure both your microphone and camera are selected and ready to roll. When everything is set, commence recording your presentation and narrate as you go along. This way, the viewers can effortlessly follow your explanations alongside the visuals. Once you're done, simply stop the recording and save your video. It's worth mentioning some key differences and considerations between these methods. Using Google slides's built-in feature tends to be more straightforward as it's specifically designed for recording presentations with the camera and audio. On the other hand, screen recording tools stand out in terms of flexibility. They offer various recording options and sophisticated editing features that give you numerous possibilities to enhance your presentation, like trimming the video or adding annotations. Regardless of which method you choose, paying attention to audio quality is crucial. Always consider using a high-quality microphone to ensure your narration is clear and impactful. Finally, if you decide to use screen recording tools, you'll often find editing features built right in, which allow you to tweak and perfect your recording to a professional standard. Now you're equipped with the knowledge to effectively record your Google slides presentation. Enjoy the process and create something amazing.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Hi, how's everything going? If you're here, you've probably heard of Chinox's Vital Fit, the health-focused smart watch you keep seeing reviews about. I've been using it for the past few weeks and in this video, I'll tell you in a simple way how it went for me. Quick heads up before we start, buy it only from the official website. There are very poor quality copies out there and they can be a real letdown. To save you the search, I'll leave the link in the description and pin it in the first comment. Let's get to the point. What is Chinox Vitalfit? It's a health-centric smart watch that puts some impressive measurements on your wrist. A 60-second ECG to see your heart's electrical activity, blood oxygen saturation, heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, and sleep analysis. It also adds estimated readings for glucose, uric acid, and lipids. A quick 30-second check to grab your vitals at a glance and an SOS function that alerts a contact with a single tap if anything happens. Day-to-day, it also works well as a watch. Bluetooth calls and notifications, a voice assistant, 100 plus sport modes and route tracking. Everything is saved to the app, which acts like a control panel where you can see clear history, trends, and alerts if anything goes outside your set ranges. How did it go for me? Honestly, great. Setup was quick and within 5 minutes, I had alerts for heart rate and oxygen turned on. The ECG takes about a minute and displays fully in the app. The sleep analysis nailed my restless nights and helped me tweak my schedule. For easy workouts, it tracked steps, calories, and pace without issues. Calls from the wrist sound good, and with medium screen brightness and notifications on, the battery lasted me several days. In terms of durability, it was enough that I didn't worry about water. And the 30-second quick check has become part of my morning routine to see heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen, and temperature in one go. In short, if you want to centralize health, basic fitness, and a bit of extra safety in one device, Kinox Vital Fit seems like a very complete option for the price. If you're interested, the link is in the description and pinned comment. And if you want me to test a specific feature or you have setup questions, drop a comment and I'll read it. See you in the next video.

Nvidia meantime is reportedly making its own version of that viral AI agent OpenClaw and they're naming it NemoClaw, Wired reports. They've been pitching it to companies like Salesforce, Cisco and Google. Deirdre Bosa has more now in today's Tech Check. Hi, Deirdre.
Hey Kelly, so what's really interesting about this whole thing is that Nvidia has built the most profitable lock-in strategy in semiconductor history. It all hinges on its ecosystem. Um, it all hinges its ecosystem on a software platform which is CUDA that forces developers to use Nvidia chips. But now, if the Wired reporting is correct, it's going to dismantle that on purpose and embrace open source. Now NemoClaw would be an open source chip agnostic platform for enterprise AI agents that builds on the viral success of OpenClaw. That's an agent that runs totally autonomously on your computer. The Nvidia platform would let companies deploy AI agents regardless of whether they run on Nvidia hardware. That is a key shift here. So no more lock-in, but that may actually be the bullish case. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, he took a company built on Windows lock-in, put office on the iPad, he embraced Linux, and went cross platform everywhere. The bet was that if you're the best, you don't need walls, you just need to be everywhere. That took Microsoft from a few hundred billion dollars in market cap to over three trillion. Nvidia could be signaling here that it has outgrown the playbook that has brought it this far and is getting ahead of the next shift because lock-in is already under pressure. Nvidia knows that. You've got Google, Amazon, Broadcom, AMD, they're all building custom AI chips to reduce their dependence on Nvidia. So instead of going on defense, Nvidia is actually racing to own the next layer up and that could be a really smart move here. We'll of course be watching this closely at GTC, Kelly.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: I've watched a lot of raw footage from joint practices and teams getting ready for joint practices, and here are my biggest takeaways. It might not sound right, but Russell Wilson and Malik Neighbors are actually getting along pretty well. The two of them have been spending a lot of time together in the meeting rooms and outside of the facilities, and it's showing on the field. Russell Wilson is putting the ball where Malik Neighbors can get it, and Malik Neighbors is always going to go up and get it. Their chemistry is a lot better than people want you to believe, and I think it might actually work out. Who's winning the Colts QB battle? Neither of them. And that is the reason Anthony Richardson's going to start versus the Ravens and Daniel Jones is going to start versus the Packers. They're both going to play in a pre-season game and whoever looks better is going to end up being the starting QB. And if I'm putting my money on one of them, it's going to be Anthony Richardson. Yes, he makes mistakes, but he's also the one who's making the more explosive plays. What's happening at Colts-Ravens joint practice? The Colts defense is actually getting a lot more stops than you would expect against the Ravens offense. Mark Andrews is 100% Lamar Jackson's go-to target. It's not even a question. And Michael Pittman, Josh Downs, and Tyler Warren are going to be your big three receivers for the Colts. Treyveon Henderson might be a three-down back. He's looked excellent in pass protection. He can obviously run the ball, and not only is he catching passes, but he's getting wide open. Meanwhile, Rhamondre Stevenson is fumbling. And speaking of three-down backs, Ashton Genti is not going to be leaving the field for the Raiders. We all know that he's a fantastic runner, but he's actually looked really good in pass protection, and he's already become one of Geno Smith's favorite targets. And I think there is a very high possibility he's touching that ball 25 plus times a game. Bonus tidbit, don't forget about Donte Thorton Jr. He is absolutely tearing up training camp every single day. He is getting more and more work. Shedeur Sanders is gonna be the QB for the Browns in most of the preseason. But that's not what I want to talk about. I don't care if the QB is Joe Flacco or Shedeur. Either way, we are sleeping on David Njoku. This man has been catching so many passes. And I think people forget that he had 64 receptions, 505 yards and five touchdowns last season in just 11 games. And finally, Dolphins training camp is physical as fuck. And I'm telling you right now, I'm 20 minutes from the facilities and it is hot as balls out there. But it don't matter. Tua Tagovailoa is absolutely thriving. He's completing 70% or more of his passes. He is executing on third downs and in the red zone like he doesn't usually do. And he's only thrown one interception in all of training camp. And while I know our defense is going to suck, I'm very high on the Dolphins offense this year. A-bada-bing-bada-boom. Baby.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Have you ever noticed how a cat can change your whole world just by curling up in your lap? I want to tell you a story about a little stray named Willow. She wasn't born into a loving home. Born under an old porch, shivering through cold nights, tiny mews barely heard over the rain. Willow's days were spent searching for scraps, darting away from heavy footsteps, wishing for a gentle hand. But the world can be tough for a small cat. One day, she was limping, her paw injured, hungry, and alone. That's when I first saw her, huddled behind a dumpster, eyes wide and scared, but with a glimmer, still hoping someone might help. I remember crouching down, softly calling to her, my heart pounding as she inched closer, cautious. Days of quiet visits, leaving food, just sitting nearby until Willow let me touch her. The first time she leaned into my hand, I felt her whole body sigh. I took her home, cleaned her wounds, and promised she'd never be alone again. But sometimes life isn't fair. Her injury was worse than I thought. The vet said she might not make it. I spent every night by her side, whispering that she was loved, that she mattered. For a while, she got better. She played, purring softly, curling up beside me as if she'd always belonged. One morning, I woke and Willow was gone. Quietly, in her sleep, she'd slipped away, finally safe, finally loved. I still miss her, but for a little while, she found her home. Sometimes that's all any of us need.

answer: It has been quite a weekend in the world of AI. Let's start with Alphabet. The company has awarded CEO Sundar Pichai a pay package worth up to $692 million. But the structure of that compensation is what stands out. A large portion of it is tied not to Alphabet's overall stock performance, but to whether its autonomous ventures, Waymo and Wing, increase the value over the next three years. That is about $392 million of the total pay package. Autonomy and AI-driven infrastructure are no longer experimental projects, but quite central to the company's long-term strategy. Defense AI is also accelerating. Palantir's Maven smart system is already embedded within US military operations and is designed to process real-time sensor and operational data to support battlefield decisions. At the same time, tensions between AI companies and the Pentagon are becoming more and more visible. After the US Department of Defense labeled Anthropic a potential supply chain risk, major cloud providers including Amazon, Microsoft, and Google moved to reassure customers that Anthropic's Claude model will continue to be available for enterprise workloads. Meanwhile, XAI led by Elon Musk has secured a deal to deploy its Grock model inside classified US defense systems in place of Claude. But Grock is also under scrutiny after generating racist content and false claims about the Hillsborough disaster, triggering investigations by regulators across UK, EU, and California. Now, there are also developments at Open AI. CEO Sam Altman says that the company has again delayed the launch of Chat GPT's planned adult mode, which would allow verified users to access explicit content. Open AI says it is prioritizing improvements to intelligence, personality, and proactive capabilities before introducing this feature. And from India, a development that could prove strategically significant. Sarvam AI has launched two open weight models. These are trained on Indian languages. One has 30 billion parameters and the other 105 billion. Now, the larger model claims benchmark performance comparable to Deepseek's R1 model despite using far fewer parameters. Then there's a US company called Target Hospitality. This is the same company that runs the ICE detention facilities in the US and has now signed more more than $130 million in contracts to build temporary worker housing for laborers constructing new AI data centers in rural Texas. It is a sign that AI race is now driving a massive physical build out involving land, power, labor, and infrastructure across multiple regions.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: So those who are waiting for the S25 FE, your first look is finally here. And it's coming from none other than trusted leaker OnLeaks. At first glance, the design might seem unchanged, but there are three key differences compared to the S24 FE. First, the device is noticeably thinner. Reports says it's just 7.4 mm thick, down from 8 mm on the previous model. Second, the bezels are getting slimmer, giving you more screen and a more modern look. And third, the camera design now matches the Galaxy S25 Edge, making the S25 FE look far more premium this time around. So, S25 FE is expected to retain the same 6.7 inch 120 Hz display, but this time it's switching from Dynamic AMOLED to Super AMOLED. That means we're likely looking at up to 2600 nits of peak brightness, making it far more usable in direct sunlight. Now, under the hood, it's almost confirmed that Samsung will go with the Exynos 2400, not the newer 2500, reportedly due to production constraints. Performance on the S24 FE wasn't bad, but the battery life did fall short of the regular S24, even with a bigger battery. That's mainly because it used a tone-down version of the Exynos 2400. So, with the full Exynos 2400 this time, we should see a noticeably boost in battery performance. Finally, closing the gap with the flagship S series. We've also got a selfie camera upgrade, going from 10 megapixel to 12 megapixel, which should improve detail and clarity. Plus, you're getting seven years of OS and security updates. The phone is launching with Android 16 out of the box, which means it could receive updates all the way up to Android 23. Storage wise, the S24 FE already had UFS 3.1 for the 128 gigs model and UFS 4.0 for 256 gigs. That's fast and the S25 FE is expected to continue that trend. Recently Apple announced iOS 26 bringing some major changes. iOS 26 is packed with intelligent experiences, meaningful improvements to the things you do every day, and a new design where we've also refreshed a number of system experiences and apps. However, the Galaxy S25 FE is also coming with One UI 8 straight out of the box. One UI 8 will also bring some major upgrades as well. While the One UI 8 beta is already out, the official release is along with the Z Fold 7 launch. So, S25 FE is expected to launch around October, so there's still time for more solid leaks and confirmation to come true. So yeah, if you're looking for a well-balanced phone with long-term software support and that signature Samsung polish, the S25 FE will be a smart pick. Stay tuned for more updates and don't forget to subscribe. Peace out.

Allow Strava to write will sync the data from Strava app to the Health app. Whereas allow Strava to read will sync the data from the Health app to the Strava. After making this selection, tap on allow. And now as you can see, Strava is now connected with the Health app. Here it shows a demo activity I just did before syncing. By tapping on import, I can transfer all the workout data from Apple Watch to Strava. You can import all workouts from your Apple Watch for the last 90 days to your Strava account. As soon as the import is finished, reload the activities page and you'll see your workouts on the Strava app. Here is the same activity open on my Apple Watch Series 10. And as you can see, the distance and duration is on point. The calorie burn is also accurate. Apple Watch shows my average pace is 11:53, whereas on the Strava, it shows us 11:52. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The lake gave no sign. For centuries, the waters of Iznik rippled softly against the edge of a city once called Nicaea, birthplace of Christian creed, stage for imperial councils, and grave to forgotten martyrs. Nothing in the breeze, the current, or the reflection hinted at what lay beneath. But in 2014, a drone camera flew low over the water and found a church sleeping just below the surface. 50 meters from the shore, in water barely 3 meters deep, rose the submerged skeleton of a Basilica. Its stone walls followed a familiar pattern, three aisles, east-facing aps, a square narthex, a structure from the early 5th century CE, built shortly after the first Council of Nicea had rewritten the rules of heaven. Scholars now believe it was dedicated to St. Neophytos, a young martyr said to have been killed on that very shoreline, stabbed and abandoned in the shallows for refusing to renounce his faith. The Basilica's shape suggests reverence, but its fate speaks otherwise. In the year 740, an earthquake shattered the region, temples fell, walls cracked, and this church, already fragile on marshy ground, collapsed into the lake and vanished from memory. No chronicler recorded its loss, no pilgrimage map marked its name. For 1,300 years, it lay beneath the water like a cathedral entombed in silence. But even underwater, the clues remained. In 2025, excavators confirmed its identity as the church of the Holy Fathers, possibly built near or over the site of the council itself. Around it, archaeologists found burials, eight tombs lined with terracotta tiles tucked beneath the nave and apse. Infants, children, adults, laid in sacred shadow as if hoping to sleep close to a martyr's bones. And just beyond the ruin a pendant surfaced, its face worn but still clear. St. Nicholas carried by a pilgrim and dropped in reverence or fear. Yet the past here is layered. Beneath the Basilica, some believe are the foundations of a forgotten Apollo temple. Others whisper of a Senate palace where emperor once spoke of salvation. And still others suspect the site predates all of them, a shrine built atop a necropolis, where holiness was measured by how long the dead had waited. No inscriptions remain, no relics speak. Only stones pressed flat by silt and time, held in place by the lake's stillness. But when drought comes, as it has in recent years, the water recedes, the basilica rises again. Columns break the surface, the apse returns to light. For a brief moment, the church is no longer drowned, just exposed. Plans exist now for an underwater museum. Glass walkways suspended above the nave, viewing chambers, lit vaults where visitors may pray or simply witness. But for now, it remains where it was found, submerged, weightless, intact. A sanctuary that did not fall from grace, but was carried into it.

Now, does that mean the hard hat smartwatch is automatically a scam? Not necessarily. The product may very well function as advertised and some buyers could be happy with their purchase. If you're considering buying the Hard Hat smartwatch, my advice is to do your homework first. Look for user feedback outside of the official website, check refund policies carefully and compare it to well-known smartwatch brands in the same price range. It may look rugged and tough, but until there's more independent evidence, it's best to approach with caution. So, is it legit or a scam? The truth lies somewhere in the middle. answer:
Are you hungry for the latest news and trends from the internet? Welcome to what's cooking on the internet. Your one stop shop for discovering the hottest digital delights. Hit that subscribe button and let's get cooking. 

Can a viral meme be a form of quiet protest or is it just a silly joke? I think it's a little bit of both. In a world where social media can turn even the most mundane moments into viral sensations, a new app from tech innovator James Steinberg is taking the concept of a meme to new heights. The app lets users change the background of their digital boarding pass to display a now infamous image of Vice President JD Vance as a bald, bearded baby man. It started as a joke, but it's raised some serious questions about freedom of political speech. Steinberg warns users to use at your own risk, but he's already seen hundreds of people use the app to create their own digital boarding passes. The idea for the app came after a Norwegian tourist, Mads Mikkelson, was detained by border control for hours and forced to unlock his phone, which contained the same meme. Mikkelson's entry into the country was denied, and he believed it was due to sensitivities over the doctored likeness of the V. E. Customs and Border Patrol later denied this, claiming that Mikkelson's admitted drug use was the reason for his ejection. Either way, the meme got a lot more traction, raising questions about freedom of political speech. An Irish politician even waved around a printout of the bald Vance meme in parliament while warning of American censorship and repression. In my opinion, it leads to a discussion at the heart of the issue, Steinberg says of his app. But what does this say about our society? Are we using memes as a way to comment on the absurdity of politics, or are we just using them as a way to distract ourselves from the real issues at hand? The project has the approval of Dave McNamee, the creative consultant and humorist in Los Angeles who kicked off the Vance Edits craze back in October of 2024. McName's edits, which included giving Van some more chiseled, Chad-like look, eventually racked up more than 200,000 likes and 16 million views on X. But the real question is, what's the point of all this? Are we using memes as a way to speak truth to power, or are we just using them as a way to mock and belittle those in power? As Steinberg's app continues to spread, it's clear that this is more than just a silly joke. It's a commentary on our society's obsession with social media, our willingness to use memes as a form of protest, and our desire to comment on the absurdity of politics. So, the next time you see a meme, remember, it's not just a joke, it's a reflection of our society's values and priorities.

Gimme what I want. Kerouac felt like an outsider. His family felt like outsiders, and he was always thinking, how do I fit in? Kerouac was such a figure of contradiction. There was this conservative side and this other wilder, free side. It was a constant tug of war. Sometimes what comes out in some of his works isn't sainthood. I don't think most women of this moment would be able to overlook the misogyny. As long as we're. Kerouac wanted to get out and experience something bigger, with all the savage irresponsibility that that comes with. We're so fascinated by people who live fast and burn bright. And it's not like a perfect book, but here we are all these years later and we're talking about On the Road. Would you compromise? Would you take it all straight on the thin white line On the Road's message was open yourself up to experience. Take chances, gain knowledge. He sort of laid down, this is the way I did it. Now you do it your way. Some look ahead Some look I'm going to college. I'm going to my future, seeing what more the world is like. Aw I've only seen my dad three times in 50 years. This is not an easy visit, but it's a visit I really have to do. Home is a feeling. I like to say home is where you park it. In the light I needed a book like On the Road to say, you're okay. That's why it really resonates, is because it's about trying to figure out your own road, your own personal path. It's about the trip, not the destination. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Xiaomi has introduced the wireless mouse 3 comfort edition, a more ergonomic take on its well-received wireless mouse 3 that arrived back in May. The new version keeps the same hardware, but opts for a wide, sculpted body with a contoured thumb rest for a more comfortable grip. This is a fairly lightweight clicker, measuring 11.89 cm tall and 7.55 cm wide, and tipping the scale at 65 grams. Xiaomi says the new, meticulously sculpted, asymmetrical design is optimized for various hand shapes and should provide more substantial support for the user's palm and fingers compared to its symmetrical sibling. The Pixart 1200 DPI optical sensor is nothing to write home about, but then again, this is an entry-level offering aimed at office use, and the word gaming doesn't appear once in Xiaomi's sales pitch. The dual color matched side buttons on the right side look nice, but they don't appear to be programmable. They're strictly for forward and backward navigation. Xiaomi teamed up with TTC to develop keys, and we're told they offer softer, quieter clicks. The wireless mouse 3 comfort edition also has a new, wider, silicone-coated scroll wheel with precise tactile feedback, and can be paired with up to three devices, one 2.4 GHz wireless connection and two Bluetooth channels. There's no USBC charging. Power comes from a single AA battery with Xiaomi promising months of use on a single cell.

answer: The Red Devils have officially completed the signing of Brian Mbeumo from Brentford in a sensational 50 million dollars deal. This isn't just another signing. This is a statement. This is Manchester United, once again showing the world that they are serious about rebuilding, evolving, and returning to the summit of English and European football. For the past few seasons, Brian Mbeumo has quietly yet ferociously carved out a name for himself in the Premier League. While others basked in the spotlight, Mbeumo delivered week in and week out, consistently performing against the biggest teams and rising to every occasion. From solo runs that left defenders clutching at air, to cold, clinical finishes under pressure, Mbeumo became Brentford's beacon of belief. With every goal, every assist, every moment of magic, he drew attention. And now, he has arrived at the grandest theater in world football. A product of resilience, hard work, and hunger, Brian's journey from League 2 in France to the Premier League was never paved with luxury. It was built brick by brick with a fire that now burns brighter than ever and Manchester United have just added that fire to their furnace. Tactical intelligence meets relentless energy. What does Mbeumo bring to Manchester United? In one word, balance. In the modern game, balance is everything and few understood that better than Portuguese mastermind Ruben Amorim, who, speaking about the move, had this to say. Brian Mbeumo is not just pace and flair. He is intelligence, discipline, and purpose. He brings balance to United's attack. He offers tactical width, counter-pressing strength, and decision-making in the final third. This is not just a good signing. This is a necessary one. Whether deployed as a right winger, a second striker, or even as an inverted forward cutting inside from the left, Mbeumo offers dynamism that Manchester United desperately need. He reads space brilliantly, times his runs with surgical precision, and crucially doesn't shy away from defensive responsibilities. For a side often accused of lacking coherence in attack, his arrival represents clarity and a turning point. As the deal was finalized and the documents were signed at Carrington, the excitement among the club's inner circle was palpable. Mbeumo arrived for his medical with a calm smile, not overwhelmed, not boastful, just ready. Ready for the challenge, ready for the pressure, ready to wear the badge. Standing inside Old Trafford for the first time as a United player, he looked out at the empty stands and whispered to the staff beside him. I've imagined this moment since I was a child. This is not just another stop in his career. This is the destination he's been working towards all along. The welcome of a family, the expectation of a legacy. From the club's side, the welcome was immediate and wholehearted.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: A World War II themed movie has taken audiences by storm, moving viewers to tears while earning widespread praise from critics and fans alike. Released in 2019, Jojo Rabbit has been hailed as a cinematic masterpiece, one that blends humor and heartbreak in a truly unique way. Directed by Taika Waititi, the film is a satirical coming-of-age story set during the final years of Nazi Germany. At its heart is Jojo, a 10-year-old boy who, indoctrinated by Nazi propaganda, idolizes Adolf Hitler, imagining him as his comical, imaginary best friend. But everything changes when Jojo discovers a Jewish girl hiding in his attic. This discovery forces him to question everything he believes, setting the stage for an emotional and often absurd journey of self-discovery. Viewers have described the film as a powerful blend of laughter and sorrow. One IMDB reviewer wrote, it was hilarious and heartfelt. The acting was superb, the story was thought-provoking. It was funny at times and heartbreaking at others. Another called the film moving, hilarious, tragic, admitting they had doubts at first but trusted Waititi's vision. The emotional roller coaster is real, they added, praising the film's originality and depth. I laughed and I cried, another fan confessed. This film was exceptional, one of the best I've seen this year. Waititi's comedic vision is brilliant, and the cast is phenomenal. The cast includes Roman Griffin Davis in his breakout role as Jojo, Thomasin McKenzie, Sam Rockwell, Rebel Wilson, Stephen Merchant, Alfie Allen, and Scarlett Johansson, with Waititi himself portraying a ridiculous, imaginary version of Hitler. Adapted from Christine Leunens' novel Caging Skies, Waititi initially drafted the script in 2011. Though the original version was much darker, it evolved into a black comedy that could balance satire with genuine emotion. Filming took place in 2018, and the movie premiered the following year to critical acclaim. Jojo Rabbit earned multiple awards, including the Academy Award for best adapted screenplay, making Waititi the first Marry filmmaker to win in that category. Audiences and critics have since labeled it a must watch film, especially for fans of war dramas told from a fresh and human perspective. From laughter to despair, Jojo Rabbit manages to confront the horrors of war through the innocent lens of a child, making it a standout film that resonates long after the credits roll.

At least 22 people have died and more than 80 more have been injured after a crane fell on top of a moving train carriage in Thailand. It happened near the city of Nakhon Ratchasima. It's around 160 miles northeast of Bangkok. The crane was working on a new rail construction project when it fell and struck a moving train causing it to derail briefly. The state rail authority there has said 195 people were on board. 

At least 32 people have been killed after a construction crane collapsed onto a train in Thailand. Around 80 others have been injured. The crash happened around 150 miles northeast of the capital Bangkok. Our Southeast Asia correspondent Jonathan Head joins us now from the scene. So, Jonathan, what more can you tell us about what happened?

I'm actually standing on the railway line where this happened and behind me they've moved away now using heavy cranes the crushed carriages. If I get the camera operator to tilt up a bit, you can see this is a brand new high-speed line that they're building on top of this existing railway line. And that huge crane you can see above me, that is now tilted at a really dangerous angle. Big parts of it came crashing down, crushing at least three of the carriages, setting one of them on fire. It really was a dreadful scene. They're trying to clear it up now. There are dozens of people still being treated in hospital, and the government has announced what it says will be a very fast investigation into what went wrong. But this is a highly prestigious project. This new railway line is meant to link Bangkok with China. It's part of China's Belt and Road initiative. So it's a very prestigious project and to have such a major disaster happen on it is a real blow to what for Thailand was meant to showcase its modernizing infrastructure. There have, I have to say, been other accidents like this before in Thailand. I think there'll be a lot of skepticism about what kind of action is going to follow this one.

It allows visitors to explore the campus flexibly and at their own pace. In addition to the self-guided option, Harvard also offers free student-led public walking tours. These tours last about 45 to 60 minutes and provide historical background, general information, and perspectives on student life. However, these tours are scheduled and requiring advanced registration. There are limits on group sizes and check-in is necessary. For those who prefer to explore independently, the mobile application is the main resource available. It is particularly useful for visitors who arrive late to the in-person tours. The Harvard University Visitor Center is located at the Smith Campus Center on Massachusetts Avenue in Cambridge. It is open Monday through Friday from 9:00 in the morning to 5:00 in the evening. This center serves as the starting point for tours and is a resource for visitors with questions about the campus. Harvard is easily accessible by public transit, making it a popular destination for those interested in Boston's rich academic and cultural environment. The self-guided tour app allows visitors to experience Harvard Yard and its surroundings while fitting well into a day spent exploring Cambridge and Boston. To summarize, self-guided tours are available via a free Harvard mobile application focused on Harvard Yard. Official student-led tours requiring advanced registration and have group size limits. The visitor center is the main hub for tour information and visitor assistance. Visitors arriving late to scheduled tours can opt for self-guided alternatives. This setup provides visitors to Boston and Cambridge with multiple ways to experience Harvard University, whether through guided or independent exploration.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The Tesla Cybertruck is one of the most futuristic and talked about electric pickup trucks in the world. Built by Tesla, this vehicle completely changes what people expect from a traditional truck. With its sharp geometric design, stainless steel body, and advanced electric technology, the Cybertruck looks like something straight out of a science fiction movie. One of the most unique things about the Cybertruck is its ultra-hard stainless steel exoskeleton. This special material makes the body extremely durable and resistant to dents and damage. Tesla designed the truck to be both tough and functional, making it suitable for heavy work as well as everyday driving. The Cybertruck is fully electric, which means it produces zero emissions while driving. Depending on the model, it can come with single motor, dual motor, or tri motor electric powertrains. The top version is incredibly powerful and can accelerate from 0 to 60 miles per hour in about 2.6 seconds, which is faster than many sports cars. Another impressive feature of the Cybertruck is its long driving range. The high performance version can travel up to around 500 miles on a single charge, making it one of the longest range electric trucks available. This makes it practical for long trips, work sites, and daily use. Inside the cabin, the Cybertruck offers a minimalist and modern interior. It features a large central touchscreen that controls most of the vehicle's functions, including navigation, entertainment, and climate settings. The spacious cabin can comfortably seat up to six passengers, making it both a family vehicle and a powerful work truck. The truck also offers strong towing and payload capabilities. It can tow up to about 14,000 pounds and carry heavy cargo in its large rear bed, which Tesla calls the vault. The bed also includes a powered cover to protect cargo and improve aerodynamics. In terms of technology, the Cybertruck comes equipped with Tesla's advanced driver assistance features. This includes autopilot, which can help with steering, acceleration, and braking on highways. Future updates may also enable more advanced self-driving capabilities through software updates. Overall, the Tesla Cybertruck represents a bold step into the future of electric trucks. With its unique design, powerful performance, long range and advanced technology, it stands out as one of the most innovative vehicles Tesla has ever created.

answer: I want to talk about something that's rarely discussed, but urgently needs our attention, Balochistan. And let's be clear, targeting the powerless, those who work far from home just to feed their families, is an act of pure cowardice. Yes, Balochistan is rich in resources, but poor in opportunity. Economic projects have brought outsiders in, creating tension. But does that justify murder? Absolutely not. The state, for its part, has promised action, but the cycle of violence, militant attacks, then harsh crackdowns only breeds more resentment. Ordinary people are caught in the crossfire, living in fear. So, what's the answer? Justice, yes, swift, fair justice, but also unity. We need to stand together, speak out against all forms of hate, and demand peace for Balochistan. Because as long as we let hatred divide us, nobody wins. Let's raise our voices. Let's demand an end to this tragedy. #StopBalochistanViolence.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer:
What announcement led to the Berlin Wall's collapse?
Imagine waking up one morning and hearing that the border you have been told is closed forever is suddenly open. That's exactly what happened on November 9, 1989, in East Berlin. A government official named Ginter Shabowski held a press conference and announced new travel rules. He said East Germans could now apply for permission to travel abroad without the strict restrictions they had known for decades. But here's the catch. He said the border would be opened immediately or without delay. No one expected such a quick change. People listening to the news thought it meant they could cross the border right away. Thousands of East Berliners flooded to the Berlin Wall, eager to see what was happening. Border guards, overwhelmed and unsure of what to do, eventually opened the gates. This spontaneous movement turned into a mass crossing, and the Berlin Wall, which had divided the city for nearly 30 years, was no longer a barrier. This announcement was part of broader reforms happening across the communist world. East Germany was feeling pressure from internal protests and from the Soviet Union, led by Mikhail Gorbachev, who was pushing for more openness and change. The East German government wanted to ease travel restrictions to calm unrest, but the public misunderstood the scope of the reforms. They believed the border was open for good, which was not exactly the plan. The fall of the Berlin Wall symbolized the weakening of communist control in East Germany and the entire Eastern Bloc. It showed that the socialist governments could no longer hold onto their strict borders or suppress demands for freedom. This event was a turning point that led to German reunification less than a year later, in October 1990. It also marked the beginning of the end for communist rule across Eastern Europe, as many countries experienced their own peaceful protests and reforms. So, the key moment was Ginter Shabowski's announcement during that press conference. It was a simple statement, but it sparked a chain reaction that changed history forever. It was the moment when the people's desire for freedom broke down the physical and political barriers that had divided Europe for so long.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Now deadly flooding in Indonesia has triggered sweeping government action against companies who are accused of worsening the disaster through deforestation. Permits have been revoked, lawsuits filed, and state takeovers threatened. But environmentalists warn the response may fall short and could even put fragile ecosystems at greater risk. After last year's catastrophic floods and landslides in Sumatra that killed more than a thousand people, officials under President Prabowo Subianto acknowledged that deforestation and overdevelopment played a major role in amplifying the disaster. Years of mining, plantation expansion, and forest fires have stripped vast stretches of rainforest across Sumatra, removing trees that once absorbed heavy rainfall and stabilized soil on steep hillsides. Dozens of companies have had their permits revoked, and the government plans to hand management of roughly 1 million hectares of land to a state enterprise. Initially, authorities indicated that the move would include the Martabe gold mine in the ecologically sensitive Batang Toru region, and conservationists have long accused the site of environmental damage. Officials now say that they are still reviewing possible violations, but critics note there's no indication development will halt in Batang Toru. Now, Batang Toru is home to the world's rarest great ape, the Tapanuli orangutan. Fewer than 800 were believed to exist in the wild before the floods. Using satellite data, experts estimate nearly 60 orangutans may have died in what they described as an extinction-level event for the species. Now, between 2001 and 2004, Sumatra lost 4.4 million hectares of forest. That's an area larger than Switzerland, making its landscapes increasingly vulnerable to landslides and flash flooding. Environmental groups warn that transferring land to state control does not guarantee better environmental practices. They say the government has yet to outline clear plans for forest recovery or long-term remediation. Now, lawsuits are seeking nearly $300 million from six companies, some funds earmarked for environmental repair. Experts argue far greater investment will be needed, and more firms may share responsibility.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: How to resize a video in Adobe Express. If you created a vertical video and want to change it to horizontal, you can do it very easily in Adobe Express. There is a resize tool, which I showed in a different video, but now I want to show you how to do it inside a project you already have, so you don't need to download and upload it again just to use the resize tool. Open the video project you created. Now you have pages in the project. Each page is a separate video. So if you have different clips on different pages, you need to resize each one separately. If you did it by accident and you want all the pages to be in the same video with different dimensions, then you need to combine them all together. Starting with one page as an example. Click on the page of the video, then click on resize at the top of the scene window. Find in the list of options the new dimension you want to change to. You can change it to whatever dimension you like. But if you need it for socials, choose one of the ready-made dimensions listed there. You have the option to resize in the current project or create a new project with the new dimensions, while the original project stays untouched. Now, if you want to change the whole video and it's split into separate pages, you can open a new page or use one of the pages you already have. Then go to the timeline by clicking it. You'll see only the timeline for that one page. The others are separate from this video. For easier access, open the same project in a different window. Now, click the other pages, open the timeline, and copy all the scenes in that video clip. Then go to the other window where you opened the first video page, add a new scene, and paste the video here. Now click resize, and you can resize the whole video like you did for the single page. When you resize the video, you only resize the window that shows the video. If you want to see the full video again or change its position, you can resize it manually inside the new dimension or resize it back to the full video as it was before changing the dimensions. To make it easier when you want to create the same video in different dimensions, you can duplicate the page where you have the full video you want to resize. Click the three dots and choose duplicate page. Now you have the same video twice in the same dimensions. Click the new page and go to the timeline of that page, although you can change dimensions from here too without opening the timeline. Click resize and change the dimensions for that video. You can change the position of the video clips inside to show the right part of the scene. When you go back to pages, you now have the same video twice and you can download them as separate videos with different dimensions. If you'd like to learn more tricks using the video editing tools in Adobe Express, then watch this video next. Like and subscribe, and I'll see you next time.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The pain behind the silence. The root of the unrest. This protest in America didn't erupt overnight. It was born from years of quiet suffering. For decades, millions of undocumented immigrants worked silently. They labored in the fields, cleaned homes, and powered the economy from behind the scenes. Yet, their presence was always treated as temporary, tolerated, not accepted. Then, in early 2025, the US government launched a harsh campaign called the Immigration Dragnet. Raids began in areas densely populated by undocumented workers. Farmers, builders, cleaners, and families who had lived in the country for decades. Homes were stormed, workplaces were invaded. It wasn't just a legal crackdown. It was a message. This country is not yours. That campaign lit a fuse. It started in Los Angeles. A small group of farmworkers walked out onto the streets. Their eyes full of tears, their hands holding signs, their voices trembling with one message. We are human, not illegal. Soon it spread across the country. New York, Chicago, Houston, Sacramento, city after city saw waves of peaceful protesters. They weren't just speaking for themselves. They spoke for the ones who had been detained, the parents separated from children, the silent. The response was brutal. Police fired tear gas, national guard troops were deployed. Mainstream media painted them as threats, as outsiders. But the truth was simple. They were just asking to be treated as people. Dreams, fear, and the road ahead. What now? Now the question stands, where is this going? Some politicians call it a victory for law and order. Others see it as a new face of racial injustice. But for the people on the ground, this is not just about laws. It's about homes, families, and futures. This is a battle for belonging. Experts say, if the movement stays united, if their voices don't scatter, this won't be just a protest, it will become a movement. A movement that could reshape immigration policy and redefine what the American dream truly means. Because the real question is, is the American dream only for those with papers or also for those with calloused hands?

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer:
At Northrop Grumman, we use our AI factory to enable two different types of AI internally. One is what we would call enterprise AI, which is helping our users, our community be more efficient and effective leveraging AI tools. And the other is to help our engineers and manufacturing employees be more effective at testing and developing capability to put into our products, what we would call mission AI. 
It's incredibly critical for us at Northrop Grumman to have this kind of capability on-premise. Uh when we think about leveraging AI, there's a lot of different use cases and some make sense in the cloud and some make sense in shared environments and some have to exist in private or classified environment. 
At Northrop Grumman, we have uh just over 100,000 employees and every single one of them has been trained on how to leverage AI. And so when we bring this AI factory to bear, it is in support of the entire company. 
Northrop Grumman operates in what we would call a highly regulated industry. And so the ability to bring tools and capabilities like AI to bear, it's an important part of our toolkit. And there's times that we're going to do that in a commercial environment. There's times that we might do that in a federal cloud environment. The important thing is that we're able to service the needs of our employees, regardless of what they do and regardless of where they have to do it. Having a capability that we can add to our existing toolkit that enables us to use our data in a way that's private to us, to provide it to our users and leverage models and train those models in a way that's material to us, gives us a flexibility that we didn't have before. And I'm talking about like satellites in space where you can't go up and touch a keyboard and fix things. And so we've been taking advantage of that. But when it comes to the acceleration of the workforce internally, or the ability to test new capabilities in this rapidly evolving landscape of AI, we can slice off workload and provide it to our engineers and that gives them a flexibility that they've never had before. We don't have to spend a ton of energy or money building up these unique environments, we can take advantage of the one we've already put together.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: From the 12th of October 2025, the EU will introduce new border checks known as the entry exit system, EES. As a part of its plans to strengthen border security, this is a new digital border system that will change requirements for British and other non-EU citizens traveling to the Schengen area, which encompasses all EU countries except for Cyprus and Ireland. It will also include the non-EU states, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein. The entry exit system is an automated IT system designed to register non-EU nationals traveling for short stays of up to 90 days in every 180 days. It will be used every time an individual crosses the external borders of any of the following countries. When EES is introduced, you may need to create a digital record on your first visit to the Schengen area at the port or airport on arrival. This will involve submitting your fingerprints, having your photo taken, and your passport scanned at dedicated booths. This new system will be introduced in phases over the first six months, and will eventually replace the current system of manually stamping passports when visitors arrive in the EU. You will not need to provide any information before traveling. At the port of Dover, Eurotunnel and Folkestone and Eurostar from St. Pancras, EES will be carried out before departure, as is currently the case for border checks. EES may take a few extra minutes to complete, so be prepared to wait during busy times at the border once the system starts. You can check with your travel operator to find out whether EES will affect your journey. Once registered, your digital record will be valid for three years. If you enter the Schengen area again during this time, you will only need to provide one biometric, either a photo or a fingerprint, at the border when you enter or exit. For more information, visit gov.uk/entry-exit system.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer:
All right, many Minnesota based faith leaders, unions and other community groups are calling for a strike and economic blackout on January 23rd. It's in response to the Trump administration's Operation Metro surge focused on people in the country illegally. Ellen Gallas shares why some businesses are planning to participate as others still are debating whether or not to join. 
This is an idea that started small, but it's getting bigger and bigger as more organizations, unions, and businesses like this one join in. Now, it is still unclear just exactly what participation levels will be though on Friday.
At this printing press and gift shop, they're experienced when it comes to getting a message out. They sell everything from greeting cards to bumper stickers. But the owners of small business Bencht Press in South Minneapolis say they're sending a different message by closing shop Friday. We wanted to figure out a way that we could join in solidarity with other businesses and say that what is happening is not right and have our voice hopefully heard at least a little bit. It's time to de-escalate. It's part of a larger organized effort by many Minnesota unions, businesses, and faith organizations to pause economic activity Friday. They're promoting no work, no school, no shopping in an effort to de-escalate ICE activity in the area. Monday afternoon representatives from many Minnesota Labor unions publicly endorsed the strike and blackout. This group represents about 80,000 members in Minneapolis and the West Metro who work in a variety of capacities from hospitality to education. A spokesperson says they don't know how many members will actually opt out of work, but they're confident most will participate in some way. If they have to go to work, they're not going to shop. If they have to, if their kids have to go to school, they're going to find another way to show up in their community. Back at Bench Press, they say they'll still be paying their employees Friday even though they'll be closed. That message they're hoping to send will cost them money, but they say it's worth it. It's unfortunate that we have to sacrifice our money, our payroll to send a message, and that's unfortunate that money is the thing that makes people talk and think, and that breaks my heart. 
Now, it's worth mentioning that I also spoke with other business owners that are still deciding and wrestling with what to do on Friday. Some of them told me that they've already lost a lot of money over the past couple weeks, and they also want to guarantee hours and shifts to their employees. So there's a lot of factors that are weighing into these decisions. Reporting in Minneapolis, Ellen Gallus, 5 Eyewitness News.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The cheetah, a sinonyx jubatus, is a large cat known as the fastest land animal in the world. It has a slender, aerodynamic body built for speed with long legs and a deep chest. Adult cheaters have tan or pale gold fur covered with small, solid black spots all over their bodies, except for the white throat and belly. One distinctive feature is the black tear marks that run from the inner corners of their eyes down to their mouths, which help reduce glare from the sun and aid in focusing on prey. Cheetahs can reach speeds of 93 to 104 km/h, 58 to 65 miles per hour in short bursts covering distances up to 500 m. Cheetahs reside mainly in various habitats across Africa and Central Iran, such as Savannas and arid mountain areas. They play an important role in their ecosystems by controlling prey populations and helping maintain balance. Unlike other big cats, cheetahs have semi-retractable claws which give them better grip, similar to track spikes on running shoes. They primarily hunt during the day and rely on their exceptional eyesight to spot prey from a distance.

answer: Let's take a look at these Adidas men's daily shoes and these are nothing fancy, just the way I like. They just look like a basic skate sneaker with a flat bottom and a wide rubber outsole. Let's put these alongside a pair of Vans. Both are the same size 10 and a half.
