question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Each year in late August, Nevada's Black Rock Desert transforms into a temporary city called Black Rock City. What began in 1986 as a small bonfire gathering on a San Francisco beach is now a global cultural phenomenon. Today, over 70,000 people arrive with tents, bicycles, and art, building a community from nothing but dust. Burning Man isn't just a festival. It's a community shaped by 10 guiding principles: radical inclusion, self-reliance, and self-expression among them. Participants wear futuristic costumes, glittering masks, and LED lights. Strangers become friends, and the desert becomes a place of freedom, creativity, and unity. The playa is a living art gallery. Giant wooden temples tower over the desert floor. Mechanical dragons breathe fire, and surreal neon structures glow against the night sky. Art cars, transformed into moving sculptures, carry dancers and lights through the dust. Everything here is created by participants, and nothing is left behind. From sunrise yoga and meditation to all-night raves, Burning Man pulses with sound and movement. DJs spin under laser beams, drummers pound in circles, and fire spinners light up the night. The energy is raw and electric, a celebration of music, creativity, and life itself in the middle of the desert. At the festival's peak, the Man, a towering wooden effigy, is set ablaze in front of tens of thousands. Flames rise, sparks scatter across the desert sky, and cheers echo through the playa. Another sacred fire consumes the temple, a space for reflection and remembrance. And then, just as quickly, Black Rock City disappears, leaving only dust, memories, and the spirit of Burning Man.

answer:
That's the final day of the UN's climate change summit, COP 30 in Brazil. Yesterday, the conference had to be evacuated after a fire broke out inside the venue. More than 190 countries have been at the summit in an attempt to strengthen international efforts to address climate change. And on this final day, the delegation from Colombia say that more than 30 countries have signed a letter opposing a draft text because of it fails to refer to the phasing out of fossil fuels. Here's our climate editor, Justin Rowlett. 

The fire is really burning very intensely, burned a huge hole in the roof. The summit was halted yesterday afternoon when a fire broke out in the venue. The intense blaze was swiftly brought under control, but it meant yet another delay in these already fraught talks. They are as much about who isn't here as who is. Secretary General, what message do you want this conference to send to Donald Trump? We are waiting for you. Hope is the last thing that dies. He urged the summit to take bold action. One thing is clear. We are down to the wire and the world is watching Belem. But when the Brazilian President, Lula de Silva flew in, signs of agreement were proving elusive. These talks are being held behind closed doors. The most contentious issues, how to bridge the yawning gap between what countries say they'll do and what the science says is necessary to avoid the worst effects of climate change and how to get rich countries to deliver on promised cash to help poorer countries play their part. The big challenge as always at these talks is that the countries here can't force the others to actually do anything. So if a country doesn't want to phase out fossil fuels rapidly, for example, they don't have to, which means that the outcome of these summits is inevitably always a compromise. And if that compromise isn't ambitious, well, there will be questions about how effective this entire global process is. Justin Rowlett, BBC News, Belem.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Liverpool's center-back plan is taking shape, and the next name on the board is Giovanni Leoni. At just 18, the Parma defender burst onto the Serie A scene last season, earning an Italy U21 call-up and a reputation for ice-cold composure beyond his years. Now, as reports suggest Liverpool are weighing a move, Anfield could become the stage where Leoni levels up from prodigy to Premier League force. Leoni is a modern center-half, aggressive in duels, calm in build-up, and brave enough to split lines under pressure. He steps in front with timing rather than rashness, angles his body to show forwards into traffic, and when he wins it, his first pass is forward. Aerially, he competes, but his standout traits are anticipation and recovery pace, perfect for a high defensive line that lives on front foot pressing. Think, win it early, play it early. Why Liverpool, why now? The Reds want at least one center back before the September 1st deadline. Jarrell Quansa has departed, Joe Gomez is nursing an Achilles issue, and Ibrahima Konate is in the final 12 months of his deal. That left Virgil Van Dijk and Konate as the only senior options for the community shield. Depth is not a luxury. It's a necessity. Leone offers upside today and headroom for tomorrow. The market picture? Italian reports float a fee around 30 million euros plus bonuses. Inter have long been viewed as favorites. Christian Chivu, who coached Leone at Parma, now sits in the Inter hot seat. Yet indications are the player would be open to Liverpool if the Reds firm up interest. Parallel to Leoni, Liverpool remain keen on Crystal Palace captain Marc Guehi, himself in the final year of his contract. Guehi brings Premier League certainty. Leoni brings elite potential at a friendlier price point. Two targets, two timelines, both fit a smart rebuild. On the pitch under Arne Slot, imagine Leoni on the right of a back two or easing in as a rotational starter. In possession, he can step into midfield to create a plus one, feed the number six, or fire diagonals to the far side winger. Nothing is done yet. Inter are watching. Palace's stance on Guehi will move the chessboard. But if Liverpool choose the high ceiling route, Giovanni Leoni ticks the boxes. Technique, temperament, and tactical fit for a system built on brave defending and faster transitions. Young, fearless, and built for the press. If the Reds make the call, Anfield could be about to welcome its next defensive diamond. Welcome to Liverpool, Giovanni Leoni.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: This refinery is the first spodumene to lithium hydroxide refinery in North America. We're deploying a new technology platform that is inherently uh much more environmentally friendly and cleaner. It's a simpler process, it's a less expensive process. I'm Jason Bevan, I'm the site manager for Tesla's Gulf Coast lithium refinery just outside of Corpus Christie, Texas. Spodumene is a lithium-containing ore. It's a hard rock material that is rich in lithium. We sustainably source spodumene and bring it to site, where we then run it through a series of conveyance systems, take it through a kiln and cooler. From there, we take it through an alkaline leech and additional purification steps, take it into crystallization and produce battery-grade lithium hydroxide. Our process is more sustainable than traditional methods and eliminates hazardous byproducts and instead produces a co-product named analcime used in concrete mixes. From breaking ground in 2023 to running rock through the kiln in 2024 to start a full integrated plant startup now in 2025, we've achieved the fastest time to market for this first of its kind technology. By removing many of the traditional stage gate hurdles seen in large projects, we were able to complete feasibility, design, and construction in parallel, significantly accelerating our construction timeline. This refinery really enables us to have access to the critical minerals for energy storage, for battery manufacturing, and ultimately for EV growth. and it enables us to accelerate Tesla's mission by regionalizing supply chains for battery minerals and materials, by providing jobs, by cutting emissions from the transportation network that's required for those supply chains. It really allows us to usher in energy independence for North America.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to seamlessly share a PowerPoint presentation in a Microsoft Teams meeting. Whether you're collaborating with colleagues or presenting to clients, sharing your slides smoothly can make a big difference in how your message is received. So, let's dive right in and make sure you're fully prepared for your next virtual presentation. To begin, you'll need to open PowerPoint on your computer. This might seem like a simple step, but it's crucial as it sets the foundation for everything that we'll do next. Once PowerPoint is up and running, go ahead and navigate to the specific presentation that you plan to share. Ensure that everything in your slides is ready to go with any final touches or edits already completed. Being fully prepared at this stage will make the sharing process much smoother. Next, look towards the top right corner of the PowerPoint window where you'll see a button labeled share. Clicking this button is the gateway to distributing your presentation, so make sure to locate it accurately. Once you've clicked on the share button, a menu of options will appear. What you need to do here is simply click on copy link. This option will generate a shareable link to your presentation, making it easy for others to access it directly. After selecting copy link, you'll be prompted to click the copy button. This step is vital as it places the link onto your clipboard, ready to be pasted wherever you need it. Now, with your link copied, you're ready to move on to the final step, sharing it with your teams. Open your Microsoft Teams application and choose the specific meeting or chat where you'd like to present your PowerPoint. You can paste the link directly into the chat with a friendly note, letting your teammates or audience know it's the presentation you'll be discussing. Alternatively, if you're in a meeting, you might paste it in the chat section for all the participants to easily access. This simple act ensures everyone in your session can follow along with your slides in real time. By following these straightforward steps, you'll be able to share your presentation effortlessly, allowing you to focus on delivering your content effectively. Remember, being familiar with the technical aspects of your virtual tools can greatly enhance your confidence and delivery during a presentation. So there you have it. You're now equipped with the knowledge to share your PowerPoint presentation in a Microsoft Teams meeting efficiently. Thank you for watching, and don't forget to subscribe for more tips and tutorials to help you navigate your digital workspace successfully. Until next time, happy presenting.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to change the font for an entire Google Slides presentation. If you've ever spent way too much time manually updating fonts on each and every slide, I've got some good news for you. This method will help ensure your presentation has a cohesive and professional look throughout, saving you time and frustration. Let's kick things off by opening your Google Slides presentation. Once you're in, take a look at the top menu bar. You're going to click on the slide option. A drop-down menu will appear and from there, you'll want to select edit theme. If you're using an older version of Google Slides, this might be referred to as edit master, but don't worry, it functions in the same way. Once you've accessed the theme editor, you'll see a sidebar on the left side of the screen. Here, you'll notice a series of slide layouts, but what you'll want to focus on is the topmost slide, often referred to as the master layout. Clicking on this slide is crucial as it governs the font and style choices for your entire presentation. Now, with the master layout selected, let's move on to the next step. Look for any text boxes within this slide and select one. You'll then navigate to the toolbar situated at the top of the screen, where there's a whole array of fonts waiting for you. Select the font that best suits your presentation style or your personal preference. Remember, the font you choose will be applied to the whole presentation, so make sure it reflects the tone you want to convey. You'll want to repeat this process for other important layout types. This might include titles, body text, or any other specific layout that's essential to your presentation structure. By ensuring each layout type has your desired font, you'll maintain consistency across your presentation. Once you're satisfied with your selections, it's time to close the theme editor. Simply click the X or close button. You'll find that the new font style automatically applies to all slides that use that particular layout without any additional steps. And there you have it. Your entire deck now has a clean, unified font style, saving you from the hassle of manual edits on every slide. It's really that simple. By following these steps, you not only ensure your presentation is polished and professional, but you also free up your time to focus on content rather than formatting. Thanks for tuning in and I hope you found this tutorial helpful. If you did, don't forget to like, subscribe, and hit the bell icon for more tips and tricks. See you in the next video.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Lenovo has officially started teasing its upcoming Legion Y700, which is set to launch in March. The company claims the device features a new AI powered network acceleration system that can reduce game latency by 54.8% in complex network conditions. The tablet also lowers in-game stutter rates by 42.7% compared to rival models, according to Lenovo's internal data. The Legion Y 700 introduces a dedicated acceleration channel for gaming. Lenovo says the AI engine detects congested or unstable network environments and prioritizes real-time gaming traffic to reduce packet loss and jitter. The tablet supports a 2,640 Hz touch sampling rate. The display is tuned for ultra fast response allowing for near instant input detection. The company describes it as instant touch, instant response, reinforcing the tablet's focus on performance gaming. The Legion Y 700 will feature an 8.8-inch 3K+ LCD display with a resolution of 3,040 by 1,904 pixels, a 165 Hz refresh rate, and 12-bit color depth. The screen supports up to 800 nits of peak brightness and the DCI P3 wide color gamut. The 165 Hz refresh rate reduces the refresh interval to 6.06 milliseconds compared to 6.94 milliseconds at 144 Hz and 16.67 milliseconds at 60 Hz, resulting in lower input latency and improved motion clarity during gameplay. The Lenovo Legion Y700 Gen 5 will be powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset. The tablet is expected to launch in multiple variants including 12 GB plus 256 GB, 16 GB plus 512 GB and 24 GB plus 1 TB configurations. It will feature a 50 megapixel rear camera with an RGB ring light and pack a roughly 9,000 milliamp hour battery. The retail box will include a 68 watt fast charger and the device is also set to come with dual USB C ports. While it's not Lenovo's first AI enabled product, this is its most aggressive attempt to blend AI into the gaming tablet experience. The Legion Y 726 will be available in black and white colors.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Welcome back to Voltage Learning. Let's walk through this Intel analog engineer question because it touches on a very common bring-up issue that trips up even experienced designers. The question asks, during bring-up, an op-amp configured as a voltage follower shows an output that rails high even when the input is at mid-supply. Which condition most commonly causes this behavior? At first glance, this can feel confusing. After all, a voltage follower is supposed to simply mirror the input. But the key insight here is that negative feedback only works if the op-amp is operating within its valid input range. Even though the circuit uses feedback, the op-amp's input pins still must stay within the device's input common mode range. If the input voltage exceeds that range, often because the op-amp is not rail to rail on its inputs, the internal input stage can saturate. When that happens, the feedback loop effectively breaks down. The op-amp can no longer regulate properly, and the output often slams into one of the supply rails, frequently the positive rail during bring-up. Now, let's briefly rule out the other options. High open loop gain is normal and expected. It doesn't cause an output to rail by itself. Slew rate limits how fast the output can move, not where it settles in steady state. And a lighter output load actually makes it easier for the op-amp to drive the correct voltage, not harder. So the correct answer is, the input common mode exceeds the op-amp's valid range. This is exactly the kind of issue that shows up during early lab bring-up and silicon validation. Intel interviewers like this question because it tests whether you understand that data sheet limits still apply, even in seemingly simple configurations like voltage followers. If you want analog explanations grounded in real world debug scenarios, not just textbook theory, that's what Voltage Learning is built to deliver.

answer: NATO leaders have agreed to significantly increase defense spending and reaffirmed their commitment to collective defense during a summit in The Hague, Netherlands. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte acknowledged the difficulty for European countries and Canada in meeting the new target but insisted it was necessary given current global threats.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Once upon a time, in the wild landscapes of Tasmania, lived the thylacine, also called the Tasmanian tiger for the dark stripes across its back. Despite its wolf-like face, the thylacine was actually a marsupial, carrying its young in a pouch, just like kangaroos. It was the largest carnivorous marsupial of modern times, a shy and nocturnal hunter that fed on small animals and birds. Unlike dogs or wolves, its jaw could open to an astonishing 80 degrees, giving it a fearsome bite. Sadly, European settlers saw the thylacine as a threat to sheep and livestock. By the late 1800s, there were even government bounties that encouraged hunting. Disease, habitat loss, and competition with dogs only made things worse. The last known thylacine lived in Beaumaris Zoo in Hobart. Filmed in 1933 by naturalist David Fleay, it died just three years later, in 1936. That moment marked the end of a species that had survived for thousands of years. Today, the thylacine remains a powerful symbol of extinction and a reminder of the importance of protecting endangered wildlife before it's too late.

answer: Rescue and relief efforts continued on Friday in Taiwan after Super Typhoon Ragasa flooded a lake above a small town on its remote east coast. Ragasa passed through the Philippines earlier this week before traveling west towards Hong Kong and Southern China. Its outer bands brought heavy rains to Taiwan's Hualien County. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: AirPods Pro 3 can connect to two devices simultaneously, but play audio from only one at a time. Auto switching enables seamless transitions between devices that share the same iCloud account. When you start playing audio on one device, the AirPods automatically switch from the other. This feature works best with Apple devices like iPhone and MacBook. The technology relies on the H2 chip for low latency processing and proximity sensors to detect the active device quickly. Important note, auto switching doesn't support simultaneous audio from both devices. There is a brief pause during each transition. For manual switching, when devices aren't on the same iCloud account or when you need more control, you can switch connections directly. On iPhones and iPads, access AirPods settings through the control center or Bluetooth settings. Simply select the device you want to connect to from the available options. The process is similar on other Apple devices like iPads where you navigate to Bluetooth settings to manage connections. For non-Apple devices, manually disconnect from the current device in Bluetooth settings and then reconnect to the desired one. Keep in mind that auto switching works most reliably within the Apple ecosystem. Frequent manual switching can reduce battery life by 5 to 10%.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: What is the Rio de Janeiro International Film Festival? Have you ever wondered what makes the Rio de Janeiro International Film Festival so special? This festival, also known as Festival do Rio, is Brazil's largest film festival and one of the most significant events in Latin America. It started in 1999 when two earlier festivals merged to create a more streamlined event. The Rio Cine Festival, which began in 1984, and the Mostra Banco Nacional de Cinema, founded in 1988, combined to avoid scheduling conflicts and make the festival experience better for everyone. Festival do Rio takes place in the vibrant city of Rio de Janeiro. Each year, it showcases a diverse selection of films, typically featuring over 350 films from more than 60 countries. You can expect to see a wide range of genres, including feature films, documentaries, and short films. The atmosphere at the festival is warm and inviting, making it a great place to enjoy both international films and a broad spectrum of Latin American cinema. One of the standout sections of the festival is called Premiere Brasil. This part focuses specifically on Brazilian cinema and is quite competitive. It features a significant number of Brazilian films, including fiction, documentaries, and shorts. This section provides a fantastic platform for local filmmakers to present their work to both local and international audiences. Attendees often have the chance to meet filmmakers and actors, which adds to the festival's charm. The audience also gets to vote for the best films in various categories, while an official jury awards the festival's main prizes, including the coveted Redentor trophy. The festival is held across multiple cinemas in Rio de Janeiro, making it accessible to a broad audience. In addition to film screenings, Festival do Rio often includes debates, special sessions, and lectures. These events contribute to the cultural and audiovisual development of the city. The festival plays a vital role in strengthening Rio's position in the audiovisual sector and promoting Brazilian culture on both national and international stages. Overall, the Rio de Janeiro International Film Festival is a major cultural event that celebrates cinema, supports local filmmakers, and connects audiences with both global and regional film production. If you are a film enthusiast or just curious about cinema, this festival is definitely worth checking out.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: What is the Adidas Firebird tracksuit? Have you ever wondered how a simple tracksuit became a cultural icon in hip-hop fashion? The Adidas Firebird tracksuit is a perfect example of this phenomenon. Originally launched in the 1980s, this tracksuit features the iconic three stripes along the sleeves and pant legs. It evolved from earlier Adidas styles, such as the Beckenbauer tracksuit, and quickly became a symbol of athletic excellence and street style. The Firebird tracksuit typically consists of a zip-up jacket and matching pants made from shiny polyester fabric. This sleek and sporty look made it a favorite among athletes and fashion enthusiasts alike. In hip-hop culture, the Firebird tracksuit holds a special place as a cultural emblem. During the 1980s, it became closely associated with the emerging hip-hop scene, especially among B-boys, MCS, and break dancers. The tracksuit was embraced for its comfort and durability, which suited the dynamic movements of breakdancing and the expressive fashion of hip-hop artists. One of the most significant moments linking the Adidas Firebird tracksuit to hip-hop came from the legendary rap group Run-DMC from Queens, New York. They famously wore the Firebird tracksuit as part of their signature look, pairing it with Adidas Superstar sneakers and gold chains. This image became iconic and helped establish the tracksuit as the unofficial uniform of old-school hip-hop. Run-DMC's 1986 hit, My Adidas, celebrated the brand and its connection to their identity. This song led to the first major endorsement deal between a music group and a sportswear company, marking a turning point in both music and fashion. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Here's how to get the best fit with your AirPods Pro 3 so you can experience ideal sound quality, optimal noise cancellation, and accurate performance from the heart sensors. Your AirPods Pro 3 come with medium-sized ear tips already attached. If you've previously owned another AirPods Pro model, it's important to know that the ear tip sizes are different for AirPods Pro 3, and you might need to use a smaller or larger size. You can find additional ear tips under the paper insert beneath your AirPods case. The sizes are labeled on the packaging and range from extra extra small to large. You can also check the size by unrolling the edge of an ear tip and checking for the size etched on the side, near its base. First, try on your AirPods with the medium-sized ear tips attached and positioned so that the heart sensors are facing forward. Gently press your AirPods in your ears and rotate the stems toward your face. The fit should feel snug and secure, and the heart sensor on the side of each AirPod should make good contact with the skin on your ear. If the fit is too loose or causes excessive pressure in your ear, try another ear tip size. You can remove an ear tip by gripping it with your fingers near its base where it's attached to the AirPod and pulling straight out using steady pressure. If you need more grip, use a clean, lint-free cloth to help you remove the ear tip. If you need a different grip, roll the edge of the ear tip inside out, then grip both sides of the ear tip firmly with your fingertips and pull straight out using steady pressure. To attach an ear tip, align it with the oval-shaped connector on the AirPod. Then, push it onto the connector until you hear it click into place. Repeat this process if needed until you achieve the optimum fit. You can also take an acoustic seal test using your iPhone to confirm you're getting the best sound quality and noise cancellation. In your AirPods settings, scroll down to the Fit and Comfort section. Then tap Test Acoustic Seal and follow the prompts. And that's how you get the most out of your AirPods Pro 3.

Jesse Lusader says, if Amelia wouldn't have made the call, it could be a much different story. He says a lot of risk factors come into play with seizures like traumatic injury and concerns for breathing processes. answer: Lewis Hamilton calls for Africa to take it back as F1 return debate heats up. Seven-time Formula 1 World Champion Lewis Hamilton has made headlines after calling on African nations to take Africa back from former colonial powers, including France, Spain, Portugal, and Britain. Hamilton made the comments while responding to a South African journalist who asked about Formula 1's long-awaited return to the continent. The sport has not held a race in Africa since the 1993 South African Grand Prix at Kyalami. The British racing icon revealed he has been pushing for years to bring Formula 1 back to Africa and says he won't retire until it happens. I've been fighting for the past six, seven years to get the sport back there. Hamilton said, making it clear that a race on African soil is a personal mission for him. Opening up about his heritage, Hamilton added, I'm half African. I've got roots from Benin, Senegal, Nigeria. It's something I'm really proud of. He went on to speak passionately about the continent's future, saying he believes Africa has the potential to be the greatest and most powerful place in the world because of its vast natural resources. However, he also expressed frustration about foreign influence over African economies and leadership structures. I don't like that the rest of the world owns so much of it and takes so much from it and no one speaks about it, he said. I'm really looking forward to hoping that the people running those different countries unite and take Africa back from the French, from the Spanish, from the Portuguese and the British. Hamilton has frequently visited Africa in recent years. During his 2024 mid-season break, he spent significant time in Senegal, describing the trip as heavy but deeply meaningful. He said it was important to learn history and honor the people and cultures his family roots trace back to. Beyond his activism, Hamilton is also preparing for the start of a new Formula 1 season, with the opening race set to take place in Australia this weekend. He marked race week with a shirtless Instagram post captioned, Race week, I'm ready. Off the track, Hamilton has also been making headlines for his personal life. Reports suggest he has recently been spending time with reality TV star Kim Kardashian. The pair were reportedly seen together at an exclusive desert destination near the Colorado River, close to the ultra-private Amangiri resort. The luxury hideaway is known for attracting high-profile celebrities seeking privacy with suites costing thousands of dollars per night. According to reports, Hamilton and Kardashian were spotted taking a cozy selfie before leaving in a black SUV. The sighting follows their joint public appearance at the Super Bowl last month, fueling speculation that their relationship may be getting serious. As the new F1 season begins, Hamilton is once again in the spotlight, not just for his racing ambitions, but for his outspoken views on heritage, global politics, and representation in sport. Whether it's campaigning for Formula One's return to Africa or navigating high-profile romance rumors, Lewis Hamilton continues to make an impact both on and off the track.

answer: Why do 100% of concertgoers expect peace, but some nights, drama takes center stage instead? What happens when culture collides with protest? Paris found out the hard way. Last night, the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra planned to fill Paris with classical brilliance, but the real fireworks weren't on stage. Mid-performance, pro-Palestinian activists unleashed flares inside the packed auditorium, sending smoke swirling where only music should have soared. Security scrambled, the audience froze, and the elegant hall was suddenly a battleground of ideals and orchestral chairs. The protest, demanding a boycott, halted the music not once, but three times. Imagine Beethoven interrupted by emergency sirens, tuxedos clashing with tearful shouts. Four protesters were arrested, but the show, somehow, went on, thanks to nerves of steel from the musicians. French officials condemned the chaos, reminding everyone, violence and art don't mix, no matter the cause. The Philharmonie de Paris says it'll press charges, drawing a hard line between creative freedom and confrontation. High culture met high drama, and Paris was left asking, when politics burst into the concert hall, who really gets heard?

answer: For decades, fusion energy, the process that powers the sun, has been one of science's greatest opportunities. Cracking it would give us a safe, clean, and virtually unlimited source of power. Controlling plasma hotter than the sun's core means solving physics so complex that even the fastest supercomputers struggle to simulate it. At the forefront of this effort, General Atomics researchers and international partners at the D3D National Fusion facility are using AI to push fusion research forward. The team is building a fully interactive digital twin of the D3D Tokamak inside NVIDI Omniverse. It fuses sensor data, physics simulations, engineering, and AI models, creating a virtual reactor that can quickly inform decisions. Key controls can be explored in the digital twin to refine the science before running real experiments. These surrogate models trained on decades of real-world data sets and running on NVIDI GPUs deliver accurate predictions at unprecedented speed. This is a platform to optimize reactor designs, accelerate commercial fusion, and make the sun's power programmable.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The White House just released a shocking video showing the exact moment a US military strike blew up a Venezuelan drug boat in the Caribbean. In the clip, you can see a bright flash light up the night sea as the vessel erupts in flames. According to the White House, the target was run by the Tren de Aragua gang, a group the US officially labeled a foreign terrorist organization earlier this year. 11 suspected members were killed in the attack, and the message from Washington couldn't be clearer. Smuggle drugs toward the United States and you won't make it home. President Donald Trump announced the operation just hours after warning traffickers that consequences were coming. His administration says the gang's ship was headed north with a major drug shipment, and the strike was carried out in international waters under US maritime drug laws. This isn't an isolated move. It comes after Trump sent the National Guard to help with border crackdowns and launched a counter-fentanyl strike force to target trafficking networks. It's part of a pattern of escalating military and law enforcement actions that blur the line between the war on drugs and the war on terror. On Truth Social, Trump celebrated the strike as proof of zero tolerance. While critics are already questioning the legality of blowing up a vessel without showing evidence of its cargo. And Venezuela's president, Nicolas Maduro wasted no time blasting the US, calling it an act of aggression and mobilizing warships and drones in response. Washington accuses Maduro's regime of working with cartels like the Cartel de los Soles to push cocaine into the US, while Maduro insists the US is just trying to overthrow him. The strike raises the stakes dramatically. Not only did it take place as US destroyers and even a nuclear submarine patrol the region, but it also follows the US doubling the reward for Maduro's capture and putting bounties on his top officials. The footage is unclassified for a reason. It's meant to be seen around the world. It's meant as a warning. Whether you see it as a bold defense of America or as reckless escalation, one thing is undeniable. The US just made the war on drugs very, very real on the open sea.

Meanwhile, Newcastle United made it clear last week that they are willing to pay whatever RB Leipzig demand for Sesko. Despite that, their bid isn't considered decisive at this stage. The reason, we don't know. The final decision lies with Sesko himself. The player is not rushing and wants to join a club that offers guaranteed development, regular playing time and a clear vision for his future. RB Leipzig are not pushing to sell. They are open to letting him go, but only if their asking price believed to be around 60 to 65 million Euros is met, and the player agrees to the move. While Manchester United and Newcastle are the front runners, other top European clubs have also shown interest, but they are currently behind in the race. Sesko's camp is evaluating all proposals, prioritizing the right project over just the biggest offer. For now, the transfers remain open and undecided. Expect things to heat up quickly once Sesko gives the green light, and both Manchester United and Newcastle are ready to move fast. Thank you for passing through, fans. answer: So you've seen it on the road. That angular stainless steel wedge that looks like it rolled straight out of a science fiction movie. The 2026 Tesla Cybertruck isn't just another electric pickup truck. It's a statement on wheels that challenges everything we thought we knew about what a truck should be. Whether you love it or hate it, you can't ignore it, and that's exactly the point. Starting at around $80,000 for the standard O-wheel drive model and topping out near 117,000 for the Cyberbeast True. The Cybertruck positions itself as a premium electric pickup. The exterior is built from what Tesla calls hard freaking stainless, a proprietary cold rolled stainless steel alloy that's roughly 1.8 mm thick on the doors and 1.4 mm on the body panels, Capital 1. This isn't just for looks. The material resists dings and dents far better than traditional sheet metal, Capital 1. Though you'll need to baby it a bit since it can still scratch and pick up surface contamination. The Cybertruck features steer-by-wire technology and four-wheel steering, Tech Times, making this massive truck surprisingly maneuverable in tight spaces. Under the angular body, you'll find an 816-volt battery pack with a capacity of 123 kilowatt hours, Wikipedia. Range varies from 318 to 340 miles, depending on configuration, Cars. And when you need to charge, the system can add significant range in just 15 minutes at high-powered stations. Performance is where this truck gets genuinely wild. The all-wheel drive version pumps out 600 horsepower and sprints to 60 miles per hour in just 4.1 seconds. While the top tier Cyberbeast cranks out 845 horsepower and hits 60 in a blistering 2.6 seconds, Kelly Blue Book. Yes, you read that correctly. This is a full-size pickup truck that accelerates faster than most sports cars. Both versions can tow up to 11,000 pounds and handle payloads exceeding 2,200 pounds, True car. So it's not all show and no go. Inside, minimalism reigns supreme with an 18.5 inch central touchscreen, controlling virtually everything. Torque you from climate to suspension height. Rear passengers get their own 9.4 inch screen, and the cabin features a 15 speaker audio system, Cars. The interior embraces utility over traditional luxury with durable materials designed to handle real work and play. The bed measures 6 ft by 4 ft with 67 cubic feet of cargo space, Cars Direct, and the composite construction keeps things practical. There's even a wade mode that lets you cross water up to 2 and a half feet deep, Wikipedia. Perfect for those off-road adventures. Safety tech includes adaptive cruise control, automatic emergency braking, and blind spot monitoring, True car, with Tesla's full self-driving system available as an $8,000 option. The Cybertruck represents Tesla's bet that the future of trucks doesn't have to look like the past, and whether that gamble pays off depends entirely on whether you're ready to embrace something radically different.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The VDNKH robot, the Soviet Android dream. Soviet engineers created humanoid robots in the 1950s that could perform 18 different commands, see, hear, and interact with amazed exhibition audiences. The VDNKH robot represented the Soviet Union's early venture into humanoid robotics and technological showmanship. Developed by young technicians under Boris Vasilenko's guidance, these robots were designed to demonstrate Soviet technological capabilities at the famous VDNKH exhibition center in Moscow. The most advanced model stood 1.8 meters tall and could execute 18 different commands via radio control, including movement, gesture recognition, and basic interaction. These robots featured primitive vision and hearing capabilities using sensors to detect light and sound for responsive behavior. The VDNKH robots performed every two hours on a special stage built in front of the electrification pavilion, drawing crowds of amazed visitors. Beyond their mechanical functions, these robots symbolized Soviet optimism about the future, representing a vision where automation would support human progress. The project combined engineering innovation with theatrical presentation, capturing public imagination about human-machine collaboration. Soviet robotics development extended beyond exhibitions. By 1980, the USSR operated over 6,000 industrial robots, representing more than 20% of the world's total. The country pioneered planetary rovers, developing the first lunar rovers and Mars exploration vehicles. While primitive by modern standards, the VDNKH robots played a significant role in robotics history, demonstrating early concepts of autonomous behavior and human-robot interaction that would influence future development.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Seeing a red light on your AirPods Pro 3 charging case, it's a signal from the case's LED indicator about the charging or battery status. A solid red light usually means the case battery is critically low, below 10%, and needs charging. If you see a flashing red light, this often indicates a charging error, potentially due to a faulty lightning port, incompatible charger, or an internal issue. While charging, the light should turn amber/orange, indicating normal charging, and then green when fully charged. Basically, the red light is a diagnostic indicator to alert you of a problem with power or charging. If you encounter a red light, first try resetting your AirPods via the Bluetooth settings on your paired device. Next, clean the charging port with a soft dry brush to remove any debris that might be interfering with the connection. Then, use a different charging cable and adapter. Ideally, use Apple's USB-C to lightning adapter as the Pro 3 supports both lightning and USB-C magsafe. Also, ensure your AirPods Pro 3 firmware is up to date via your paired iOS device. If the red light persists, it might indicate a hardware fault. In that case, contact Apple support or an authorized service provider, especially if the device is still under warranty, which has been extended to two years in some cases due to reported manufacturing defects.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: In April 1976, six years after the Beatles' official breakup, an unusual moment in television history nearly triggered a legendary reunion. Lorne Michaels, the newly appointed producer of Saturday Night Live, made a bold and humorous pitch during a live broadcast. Looking straight into the camera, he offered the Beatles $3,000 to reunite on the SNL stage and perform three of their classic songs. Holding up a check, Michaels jokingly added that the money could be split however they wished, even suggesting that if they felt Ringo Starr didn't deserve an equal share, they were free to divide the funds accordingly. The proposal was clearly meant as satire, but fatefully, two of the Beatles, John Lennon and Paul McCartney, were watching the show that very night. McCartney happened to be visiting Lennon at his Dakota apartment in New York City, only a short cab ride away from the NBC studio. According to various sources, including Tom Doyle's Man on the Run, the two icons laughed heartily at Michael's stunt. Lennon, amused, turned to McCartney and suggested, half-jokingly, "Should we go down there and just do it?" They were reportedly close to calling a cab, but ultimately decided against it, citing the late hour and their desire to relax. It was a near miss that fans have since romanticized as the Beatles reunion that almost happened. Although Lennon and McCartney didn't follow through, the moment lived on as a curious what if in pop culture. Later that year, George Harrison appeared on SNL's cold open. In a scripted bit, he confronted Lorne Michaels to claim the $3,000. Michaels explained deadpan that the offer was intended for all four members and that Harrison alone was only entitled to $750. Harrison, staying in character, haggled for an extra $250 if he agreed to say the famous line, "Live from New York, it's Saturday night." This whimsical series of events has become a cherished anecdote among Beatles fans, capturing a moment when a spontaneous, lighthearted invitation nearly brought together two of the world's most influential musicians. It stands as a testament to the Beatles' enduring presence in the public imagination and how even the most casual of gestures can ripple through music history.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Your AI agents are burning tokens like crazy and it's not your prompt's fault. It's the architecture. Anthropic just dropped the biggest update yet, MCP code execution, and it changes everything about how agents work and can save up to 98% tokens. I'll explain what's new, why MCP needed this upgrade, and I'll show you a real demo that anyone can run locally. Typically, every MCP server exposes 10 to 20 tools. Every tool comes with function description, parameters, types, examples that translates into tens of thousands of tokens. All irrelevant for 90% of tasks. And this is where accuracy drops because the model is drowning in noise. It keeps confusing tools, mixing parameters, hallucinating schema fields, and failing mid-workflow. This is the new mental model behind MCP. Instead of dumping every tool definition into the model's context window, tools appears as a file system. To get the exact estimates, I generated a synthetic cloud watch style data set that looks exactly like what real DevOps engineers deal with. So, it has data for 150 EC2 instances. Each instance has 50 to 150 CPU data points. What the script does is loads the entire data set as raw text. This means all 18,000 data points become part of the prompt. The LLM has to read the entire JSON block. This turns into 355,000 tokens, which is almost double of what the token limit of the LLM is, and ultimately the LLM is choked. It throws a quota exceeded error where the limit is just 125,000 tokens. Now, let's take a look at the MCP style flow, where the model doesn't touch the data set. We filter the data set locally. The local Python finds the high CPU instances. Only the tiny summary is passed into the model. Gemini responds instantly. Token usage drops from 355,000 to 2096. That's more than 98% token savings. And this is the magic. The LLM sees only the result, not the 18,000 data points. This is why MCP code execution is such a big deal. Instead of forcing LLMs to parse huge tool definitions and giant JSON blobs, we let the model write code on which it is exclusively trained on, and we only give it the tiny slice of data it actually needs. Let me know in the comments what you think about MCP code execution. See you in the next video.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Manchester City star Erling Haaland has finally given fans a rare glimpse into his private life, and it's nothing short of heartwarming. The 25-year-old football sensation has launched his brand new YouTube channel, and in his very first video titled Day in the Life of a Pro Footballer, Haaland opens the doors to his stunning six-bedroom mansion in Alderley Edge, Cheshire. But that's not all. For the first time, he shares sweet moments with his girlfriend, Isabel Haugseng Johansen, and their newborn baby boy, born last December. The couple who first met as kids while playing at the Bryne Football Academy in Norway reminisce about their early days together. Haaland jokes that Isabel was a good footballer, even comparing her to Manchester United legend Ryan Giggs, saying, left wing, swinging them in. Laughing, Isabel replies, I wasn't the best dribbler, but I had speed a bit like you. In the video, the pair's chemistry shines through as they cook dinner together, tomahawk steaks with potatoes, a bearnaise sauce, and a fresh tomato salad. Haaland admits he was surprised by how good her sauce turned out, laughing, better than I thought, very good sauce. The film also dives into their love story, revealing that Isabel once liked one of Haaland's friends before she changed her view after seeing him. She calls it fate, but Haaland playfully disagrees. The Norwegian striker also references his old viral rap video from his teenage years when he performed as part of the group Flow Kings, rapping and holding BBQ utensils in a playhouse, something Isabel remembers watching back then. Since then, their bond has only grown stronger. From yacht holidays in Ibiza to fashion events in Rome, Isabel has become a quiet but steady presence in Haaland's life, always there to celebrate his victories, both on and off the pitch. And now, with his YouTube debut, fans are finally getting to see a softer, more personal side of the Manchester City superstar, not just as a goal machine, but as a proud boyfriend, a new father, and a man who's clearly loving life. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Experiencing random chimes, beeps, or haptic feedback on your AirPods Pro 3? These are often linked to firmware glitches, mode switches, or customizable features. The good news is, most of these can be resolved. Chimes or beeps usually indicate events like low battery or pairing, while haptic signal mode changes, such as active noise cancellation turning on or off. Random triggers can be caused by environmental factors, such as wind detection triggering mode switches, or software bugs like accidental Siri activation. To stop them, start by updating your AirPods firmware via settings, general, software update, ensuring your AirPods are connected. If problems continue, move on to the next section to further troubleshoot and stop these disruptions. Now that you know where these sounds come from, let's fix them. Open your iPhone settings and navigate to accessibility AirPods. Here, you can disable specific sounds like play sound on mode change to stop beeps when switching between ANC and transparency. For more aggressive solutions, try resetting your AirPods. Hold the force sensor on both earbuds for 15 seconds until the status light flashes amber, then re-pair them with your device. As of the latest updates, including iOS 18.1, you may also have an AirPods Control Center widget for quick alert management. If issues persist, consider third-party apps for fine-tuning haptic intensity or muting Siri prompts. By following these steps, you can minimize unwanted noises and customize your AirPods Pro 3 experience.

Open the Find My app to verify that spatial audio and personalized features function correctly. For an extra check, use third-party apps like AirBattery to verify compatibility, but be cautious as unofficial tools may pose a malware risk. Combining physical and digital checks gives you the best chance of identifying fake AirPods Pro 3.

We're here today because Governor Morrisey has issued a order that has our state police and our county police helping the federal government help Ice go into communities when they should be in our own communities taking care of us. answer: Good morning and thanks for joining us from the SNC World Headquarters in New York. I'm Deonte Merini. Here are the top stories we're following at this hour. President Trump announced plans to close the Kennedy Center for up to two years, starting in July, for major renovations. Now, the move comes after several performers boycotted the venue following leadership changes. Trump says the upgrades will preserve the center and strengthen its future, pending board approval. A five-year-old boy and his father are back home in Minnesota after being released from federal custody. US Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained the pair last month during an enforcement action. A judge ordered their release over the weekend. The government says the father entered the country illegally, while his attorney says he has a pending asylum claim. The mayor of Portland, Oregon is demanding that ICE leave the city after federal agents used tear gas during a weekend protest outside an immigration facility. Now, the mayor called the demonstration peaceful, while federal officials have not yet confirmed details of the response. President Trump says federal agents have been instructed to aggressively protect government property during protests. A Democrat has won a short-term victory in a Texas state Senate special election. The labor union leader and veteran Taylor Remmett defeated Republican activist Lee Womgans in a Fort Worth area district previously won by President Trump. The seat is temporary with both candidates set for a rematch in the November general election. Utah Governor Spencer Cox has signed a bill expanding the state's Supreme Court from five to seven justices. Republican lawmakers say the move will improve efficiency and bring Utah in line with other states. For 24/7 news from around the world, head to snc.tv and follow us on our new Facebook page at this hour on Salem News Channel. In New York, I'm Deonte Merini.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer:
The city of Malibu is suing the state of California and city of Los Angeles over the Palisades fire. The lawsuit claims that government failures worsened the destruction. NTD's Christina Corona tells us more.
The city of Malibu is seeking accountability months after the Palisades fire tore through the community. It's asking for damages from the state of California as well as several state, county, and local agencies. In a 66-page complaint, Malibu says the wildfire destroyed more than 700 homes and dozens of businesses, leaving burn scars along the Pacific Coast Highway and damaging areas like Carbon Beach. City leaders say Malibu's entire character changed after the blaze burned down parts of the beachside community. The complaint says the fire was not an act of nature, but a result of what the city calls unlawful conduct and failures in inspection and emergency preparedness. The lawsuit claims officials prioritized protecting rare and environmentally sensitive plants over clearing hazardous vegetation near the site of the earlier Lochman fire, a burn area that allegedly reignited just days later. The city argues that state employees hindered firefighters' efforts to cut dry brush and remove fuel, even though hotspots and active burn areas were still visible. The lawsuit seeks to recover financial losses, including costs of emergency response, infrastructure repairs, environmental restoration, and lost revenue from tourism and local businesses. Malibu Mayor Bruce Silverstein says the decision to sue was not made lightly, adding that the city has a duty to protect residents and taxpayers while continuing to work with regional partners. The state of California and the city of Los Angeles have not yet commented on the lawsuit. Christina Corona, NTD News.

answer: Where does the official Harvard University visit tour start? Imagine stepping into the heart of Cambridge, Massachusetts, ready to explore one of the most famous university campuses in the world. If you're wondering where your adventure begins, the starting point is right outside the Harvard Square MBTA station. This station is part of the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority subway system, and it makes reaching Harvard easy from Boston. When you arrive, look for the Out of Town newsstand, a well-known landmark and a popular meeting spot for visitors. This small kiosk is hard to miss and serves as the official starting point for the tour. From here, most guided tours led by current Harvard students kick off. The tours usually last about 70 minutes and take you through key campus sites. You will see the iconic John Harvard statue, which is a favorite photo spot, and the historic Widener Library, home to countless books and archives. The guides share stories about Harvard's history and student life, making the experience both fun and educational. If you prefer to explore on your own, self-guided audio tours are also available from the same starting location. These allow you to walk at your own pace and discover the campus and nearby Cambridge neighborhoods. The Harvard Square area itself is lively, filled with bookstores, cafes, and shops, making it a great place to begin your visit. The station and the out of town newsstand are easily accessible by public transit. So whether you're coming from Boston or nearby areas, starting your Harvard tour here is simple and convenient. This spot is not just the beginning of your tour, but also a lively hub that captures the spirit of Harvard and Cambridge. So, when you plan your visit, remember that the official tour begins right outside the Harvard Square MBTA station, making your journey into Harvard's history and campus easy and enjoyable.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: When we were creating imagery for the Nvidia CES keynote, one of our goals was to create a high-fidelity group shot of 20 specific robots. We realized early on that a primary technical challenge was pixel density. Current generative models are limited to 4K or 5K resolution. So each robot occupied too small an area for fine detail. For this major keynote, we also needed a flexible workflow that allowed for rapid iterations without rebuilding the entire scene. Here's how we solved it. We began by generating low fidelity 3D models from reference images. While these were rough placeholders, they provided exactly what we needed to establish the initial layout for every robot in the set. Then, we brought these models into 3D software to assemble the scene. This gave us the flexibility to explore different compositions with total accuracy and control before committing to high resolution assets. Once the layout was locked, we exported the scene. While the final lighting and fine robot details weren't perfect, the scene gave us the precise coordinates we needed. We took the exact angle of every robot and went back to our reference images to generate fully detailed 4K individual assets that fit the composition perfectly. In Photoshop, we reconstructed the layout using these high-quality robot images. The result was a clean, high fidelity composition where every element was sharp and correctly positioned. Next, we used Weavy to build a custom AI agent that let us rapidly iterate on various lighting themes. Once the creative direction was settled, we generated the full 4K scene with the final look and lighting, then upscaled it to 12K. Given the complexity of generating 20 characters in a single pass, we took a targeted approach to the robot details, regenerating our high-detail robot assets specifically to match the new lighting environment and integrate seamlessly into the final composition. We brought these light-matched high detail robots back into Photoshop and merged them into the composition to restore all the lost texture and sharpness. After final touch ups to clean the scene, we produced a massive 12K high detail environment built specifically for the giant keynote screen. This workflow allowed us to handle change requests rapidly, maintain full control over the composition, look, and detail of every individual component, and bring the scene to life just as we had envisioned.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Just a year after more than 200 people were killed in Spain's deadliest floods on record, anger in Valencia still runs deep. Thousands have marched in the streets demanding justice and the resignation of the region's president over his handling of the disaster. Roads transformed into raging rivers. Cars swept through streets and stacked like toys. Homes destroyed. Last year's floods in Valencia, Spain killed 229 people, and as the first anniversary approaches, the waters may have receded, but anger at the government remains. Thousands of protesters marched through the streets demanding Valencia's regional president, Carlos Mazon, resign over his handling of the disaster, Europe's deadliest floods in over half a century. We want Mazon and his entire government to resign for failing to take responsibility for a full-blown massacre. President Mazon has been criticized for not sending out alerts until after the flooding had already started. By the time they were, for many, it was already too late to leave. It's getting worse every day. You hear him speak and it's one lie after another. I have lost three people and they were all very young. All I ask is that justice be done. Protests in the immediate aftermath of the floods became heated. Even Spain's king was pelted with mud when he visited victims. And while this demonstration was more subdued, the message was just as strong, with ongoing inquiries yet to deliver the justice victims are demanding. Patrick Murrell, 10 News.

The combination of breaking a world record and winning the gold medal makes it a remarkable feat. While her javelin performance was impressive, the hurdles truly highlighted her speed and technical prowess on the track. Babe Didrikson's performance in 1930 to remains a significant chapter in sports history. She won medals in running, jumping, and throwing events, a feat unmatched by any other track and field athlete, male or female. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Charles Coste, the world's oldest living Olympian and a celebrated cycling champion, has passed away at the age of 101. The French presidency confirmed that Coste died last Thursday, leaving behind a legacy that spanned more than a century of dedication to sport. Coste first rose to international prominence at the 1948 Olympic Games in London, capturing the gold medal in the men's team pursuit at the historic Herne Hill Velodrome. Alongside teammates Pierre Adam, Serge Blusson, and Fernand Decanali, the quartet, known as the ABCD team, won by nearly 40 seconds over Italy, marking the largest margin of victory in Olympic cycling history. His accomplishments didn't end there. Coste went on to compete professionally with the Peugeot team, claiming victory at the prestigious 1949 Grand Prix des Nations, where he defeated Italian cycling legend Fausto Coppi. Over his career, he rode in two Tours de France and four Giros d'Italia, retiring from professional cycling in 1959. After hanging up his wheels, he pursued a new path as a sales inspector for La Blanchisserie de Grenelle, Europe's largest laundry, demonstrating the same discipline and commitment off the track that had defined his athletic career. More than 70 years after his Olympic triumph, Coste returned to the spotlight as one of the final bearers of the Olympic flame for the 2024 Paris Games. In a moving moment during the rain-soaked opening ceremony, he wheeled himself into the stadium dressed entirely in white, lighting the torches of French Olympic gold medalists Teddy Riner and Marie-José Pérec. That moment symbolized the passion and spirit of transmission that drove him, Riner said. Charles Coste embodied dedication, respect, and love for sport in all its forms. Emmanuel Macron's office praised Coste as, until his final breath, the tireless messenger of a certain idea of sport, highlighting not only his athletic achievements, but also his enduring role as an inspiration to generations. Following the passing of Hungarian gymnast Ágnes Keleti earlier this year, Coste had held the distinction of being the oldest living Olympic champion, a testament to his longevity and influence in sport. From pedaling a wooden tricycle as a child near Toulon to becoming a national and Olympic hero, Charles Coste's life was defined by dedication, excellence, and the pursuit of greatness. France and the global cycling community have lost a legend, but his achievements and the inspiration he provided will be remembered forever. The President of the Republic and his wife pay tribute to the memory of this champion who left his mark on the history of his sport and of the nation, Macron's office said, offering condolences to Coste's family and cycling enthusiasts worldwide.

answer: Nicole Kidman just broke her silence, and what she said hits deep. Quote, Everyone was saying, you've got to still go and accept the award, she shared. And I just sat for a minute and said, no, I can't. I don't and I won't. Unquote. That moment said it all. Nicole was done living for what others expected. She was finally standing up for herself, saying no when she needed to, and yes to her own healing. It's a powerful message, especially coming from someone who's lived so much of her life in the public eye. After nearly two decades of marriage, raising two daughters, and balancing massive careers, Nicole's words remind us that even icons have to stop, breathe, and choose peace. As she steps into this new chapter, Nicole Kidman isn't just turning the page, she's rewriting the story on her own terms. Perfect for pros who have to deliver in both because advertising on phone screens have been increasingly popular and open gate saves us from doing double the work, shooting horizontally, then vertically, or doing that awkward vertical crop from a horizontal footage. God, this vertical crop is just too close. Bleh! I hate it. What's even worse is Canon and Nikon are starting to equip their mid-range cameras, the R6 Mark III and the ZR to shoot raw videos, which means users can change the ISO and white balance cleanly in the edit. Arguably very handy. But is it necessary? Now, Sony is choosing to have their gates closed, and I've expected that. No way the A7 Mark 5 would get open gate or even raw video for that matter. At least not before the next A7S or the next FX camera. You know what I mean? Keep in mind, this is a mid-range camera. It's not meant to have the newest cutting-edge features until its bigger brothers do. And raw video is nice, but what's not nice is the insane file size that comes with it. In order for us to manipulate the ISO and white balance in post cleanly, requires a lot of data. The new Canon R6 Mark II requires approximately 10 gigabytes per minute for a 7K 30p raw video. So if you want to shoot an hour's worth of footage, you're going to need a little more than 600 gigabytes of memory. Yikes. For the pros of pros, you guys might not mind it, but most people wouldn't need this much power, nor even have the resources to handle this much power. Would it have been nice to have? Absolutely. But Sony decided to hold back. They'll do it someday once they're pressured enough to do so, but for now, the A7 Mark 5 does not and will not have any form of open gate raw. Perhaps the A7 Mark 6, likely in 2028.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: If we are right, by the end of 2028, more of the world's intellectual capacity could reside inside of data centers than outside of them. This is an extraordinary statement to make. And of course, we could be wrong. But I think it really bears serious consideration. A super intelligence at some point on its development curve would be capable of doing a better job being the CEO of a major company than any executive, certainly me, or doing better research than our best scientists. Some people want effective totalitarianism in exchange for a cure for cancer. I don't think we should accept that trade-off, nor do I think we need to. AI should extend individual human will. We'll probably need super intelligence to help us figure out the new governance mechanisms to ensure that this happens fairly at scale and to avoid problems like extremely unbalanced compute access or something else. We need to start broadening how we think about safety to include societal resilience. No AI lab, no AI system can deliver a good future on their own. For an obvious example, there'll be extremely capable biomodels available open source that could help people create new pathogens. We need a society-wide approach about how we're going to defend against this. We don't yet know how to think about some super intelligence being aligned with dictators in totalitarian countries. We don't know how to think about countries using AI to fight new kinds of war with each other. We don't know how to think about when and whether countries are going to have to think about new forms of social contracts. But we think it's important to have more understanding and society-wide debate before we're all surprised. The vision that AI companies lay out fundamentally reduce to either unilateral control or decentralized power. Sharing control means accepting that some things are going to go wrong in exchange for not having one thing go mega wrong, cemented totalitarian control. This is a fundamental trade-off of democracy and it is one that we believe in very strongly as the way to give everyone collective agency over the future. Of course, this is not to suggest that we won't need any regulation or safeguards. We obviously do, urgently, like we have for other powerful technologies. In particular, we expect the world may need something like the IAEA for international coordination of AI and especially for it to have the ability to rapidly respond to change in circumstances. Thank you very much.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: French cyclist Charles Cost, the 1948 Olympic track cycling gold medalist and the world's oldest living Olympic champion, has passed away at the age of 101. Cost's remarkable life and enduring legacy spanned more than a century, inspiring generations of athletes and fans alike. Cost first rose to fame at the 1948 London Olympics, capturing gold as part of France's team pursuit on the track. That victory marked the start of a storied career, which included racing on the roads, with appearances in the Tour de France in 1952 and 1957. Over time, Cost became not just a champion, but a symbol of dedication, resilience, and the enduring spirit of sport. More than seven decades later, Cost returned to the Olympic spotlight in a moment that captured the world's imagination. At the 2024 Paris Olympic opening ceremony, he served as the penultimate torch bearer, wheeling himself into the stadium and passing the Olympic flame from his wheelchair to French gold medalist, judoka Teddy Riner and sprinter Marie Jose Perec. That moment, set against the rain-soaked streets of Paris, became an iconic image of perseverance, mentorship, and the timeless connection between generations of athletes. The image of him passing the Olympic flame to Teddy Ryner and Marie Jose Perec in the reign of Paris during the opening ceremony of Paris 2024 went around the world, IOC President Kirsty Coventry said. He will be remembered forever. Our thoughts are with his family at this difficult time. Cos's achievements extended beyond medals. He embodied the Olympic spirit, serving as a bridge between the post-war games and the modern era, showing the world what it means to compete with courage, passion, and humility. His presence in Paris reminded millions that the Olympic games are about more than victories. They are about inspiration, legacy, and the unbreakable bond between sport and humanity. With Cost's passing, the title of the oldest living Olympic gold medalist is now believed to belong to Nikita Simonian, a Soviet Union soccer player who competed at the 1956 Melbourne Games. Simonian recently celebrated his 99th birthday on October 12th, continuing the torch of history that cost helped light so brilliantly. Charles Cost's life will be remembered not only for the medals and records, but for the dignity, grace, and inspiration he brought to every race, every ceremony, and every athlete he touched. From London to Paris, from the track to the global stage, Cost's legacy is timeless, a story of resilience, achievement, and the enduring power of sport to inspire generations.

Ryan, progression into the next round of the Caribao Cup with victory over Preston North End. What did you make of the match?
Yeah, um I think we started the game really well. Um obviously got the goal but then once we conceded we got sloppy for 15, 20 minutes spell, but half time came at a good time. We got a good chat and um we went in the second half and showed what we were about. We kind of took the game to them, dominated it a bit and we looked like the one team going to win.
A first competitive goal in a Wrexham shirt. How did that feel for you?
Yeah, it was brilliant. Um obviously it was a, it's a good one to start off and it's a, it was a good finish. Obviously I've cut inside and only one thing on my mind, I think people that might say it was a cross, but once you get to know me, you'll know I won't cross from that area.
What's it like for you as a striker just getting that goal duck broken early on?
Yeah, it's important. Um, that's why I come here is to help the team score some goals, um get some wins and luckily we've done that today, but the most important thing was getting through to the next round.
What sort of character did it show for you to make sure that you got into that next round, especially with how late on it was?
Yeah, um, I think since I've came here, I've seen the the attitude of the group never say die and I think towards the last the last 10, 15 minutes, I thought we were going to win here. I never thought that was going to go to penalties. I don't think anyone was preparing for it. I think we thought we were going to get a goal at some point and um, thankfully it came right at the end.
It's the first time that the club have progressed into round three of this competition since 1981. Does that almost put into perspective just the growth that this club has gone on?
Yeah, it is. As you say, it's been a long time since we've been in this round. So let's hope we get rewarded by a nice draw in the next round. Um, but all we can do is when we find out who we play, is go there and go there with the mindset that we want to go even further. So that one was 81, what was it since we're at the next round. So we're going to go there and try and win as well.
What sort of confidence can this bring the group ahead of the weekend against Millwall?
Yeah, it's got to give us confidence. And I think the two, the two games that we've had in the cups been um, Championship opposition. So it's virtually been a a Championship fixture and they fielded a strong team tonight as did we. Um, so it's obviously it's breeding confidence that we can beat teams in our league. So, yeah, it's it's one that's going to give us good momentum going into the next game.
Just finally, that fan base backing you on tonight. What's your message to them as you sign off?
Uh, I said that when I went in. I said for a Tuesday night Caribao Cup game, that was incredible. Um, the fans that came, I think they almost sold out the allocation in the in their away end and it's a big one at that. It's just thanks, thanks for the support. We'll try and repay you every time on the pitch and obviously get rewarded with a late goal tonight.
Thanks, Ryan.
Cheers.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Fever is an elevation in body temperature mediated by hypothalamic pathways in the central nervous system. The hypothalamic thermoregulatory center controls body temperature through three mechanisms. One, controlling heat production mainly in the muscles and liver, two, controlling heat dissipation from the skin and lungs, and three, setting the normal body temperature. Fever is a physiologic process where the hypothalamus sets a higher body temperature set point in response to endogenous signaling. The body then rebalances heat production and dissipation to elevate the body temperature to the new set point. This is why patients with new fevers often feel cold and experience rigors. Their current body temperature, although elevated above true normal, lies below the newly elevated hypothalamic set point and leads to the subjective feeling of cold.

answer: In an unforgettable moment that instantly became the emotional highlight of her wedding day, a bride was left completely stunned when a very special, and very unexpected, guest walked into the room, a glowing, pregnant Ellie Goulding. The couple later expressed that the surprise wasn't just a highlight of the night, but one of the most meaningful experiences of their lives. They praised Goulding for her kindness, humility, and willingness to make the day unforgettable. The bride's friends admitted that pulling off the surprise required months of planning, coordination, and secrecy, but seeing the emotional outpouring from both the bride and the guests made every effort worthwhile. For the bride, the moment will be replayed in her heart forever, a dream come true, delivered by her favorite artist at the most meaningful moment of her life.

Spain, torrential rain triggered severe flooding in parts of Valencia on Monday as storm Gabriel continues to batter the region. The state meteorological agency, AEMET, extended a red alert until midday, warning of more heavy downpours with, in fact, Tarragona also under the highest alert. In the Ebro Delta alone, up to 200 mm of rain fell within just 8 hours. Emergency services were deployed across Zaragoza where rescues were carried out, including children evacuated by inflatable boats. Now streets remain swamped while cleanup of mud and debris is underway after the overnight storm. Gabriel had earlier struck Portugal's Azores islands with less intense winds and rains, though damage from toppled trees and collapsed roofs was reported. The memory of last year's devastating floods which killed over 220 people in Valencia still haunts residents, many of whom blame officials for failing to issue timely warnings. The authorities are urging vigilance as the storm system threatens to dump even more rain across Eastern Spain.
