question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Immersive tourism represents a fundamental shift in how people experience destinations, and Customer XR's Innisfree Garden tour is a clear example of this approach in action. Customer XR developed the Innisfree Garden immersive tour to give users the ability to explore the beauty of the cup gardens of Innisfree in upstate New York from anywhere in the world. The experience removes physical, financial and logistical barriers, allowing audiences who may never be able to travel to the site in person to still meaningfully engage with the landscape. At the same time, it offers travelers a powerful way to preview and understand the destination before visiting, increasing confidence and emotional connection. The Innisfree Garden experience is a fully realized product built from the ground up by customer XR's team. The process combined on location filmmaking using high resolution 360 degree cameras and custom XR development to deliver a cohesive, immersive experience. Unlike traditional virtual tours viewed on a browser or mobile phone, this experience was built for VR first, not adapted from a 2D workflow. It takes full advantage of immersive technologies that are impossible to replicate on flat screens, including hand tracking for natural interaction, stereoscopic visuals for depth and presence, and spatial audio that grounds users in the environment. These elements work together to create a strong sense of scale, atmosphere, and emotional immersion. This VR First design philosophy is what sets customer XR's immersive tours apart. The Innisfree Garden Tour demonstrates that when immersive tourism is approached as a true XR experience, rather than a passive viewing tool, it becomes more accessible, more engaging, and more memorable for users. It is a practical proof point that immersive tourism works, delivering meaningful experiences to travelers while offering destinations a powerful, future-facing way to share their spaces with the world.

The former president and first lady were met with a combination of cheers and boos as they entered the venue, a moment captured in several viral videos circulating online. According to the Associated Press, several drag queens attended in protest, taking a stand against Trump's previous comments and promises to cut drag performances at the venue. CNN also reported that a woman yelled, felon, you're a convicted felon, referencing his recent legal troubles. However, not all in attendance were critical. Others reportedly shouted messages like, we love you, showing the deeply divided sentiments among attendees. Tensions extended beyond the audience. According to CNN, between 10 to 12 performers from the production had planned to boycott the June 11th performance in protest of Trump's presence. Sources claim that the cast was given the option to sit out without penalty. Richard Grenell, Trump ally and current director of the Kennedy Center, told the outlet he was unaware of the planned boycott. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: You know, when you've lived as long as I have, you start to notice things most folks miss. Take the eagle, for instance. Majestic, proud, an old soul of the skies. I've watched eagles for decades, and every time I'm reminded of the wisdom nature holds, if you're patient enough to see it. Now, the eagle doesn't rush. It waits, circling high above, reading the wind, the world below. There's a lesson there, I reckon. Sometimes it's not about how fast you move, but how well you understand your surroundings. When the time comes, the eagle strikes with purpose, never wasteful, always precise. I remember sitting by the riverbank, cane in hand, watching an old golden eagle teach its young to fly. The little one flapped, fluttered, nervous as a leaf in a storm. But the parent watched, steady, patient, letting the eaglet learn from its own trials. Eagles don't fear storms, you know. They ride the winds, using the storm to lift themselves higher. That's something I've tried to remember when life's thrown me a gale or two. Sometimes, you've got to face the wind, spread your wings, and trust you'll soar above it all. So next time you see an eagle overhead, take a moment, watch, listen. There's wisdom in those wings, and maybe, just maybe, a little of that old magic will rub off on you too. Thanks for listening to an old man ramble. Keep your eyes to the sky. You never know what you'll learn.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: At Florida's Capital this afternoon, a Senate committee making a major change to a controversial bill that puts more restrictions on public employee labor unions. Our Capital Bureau reporter Cody Butler tells us this will create another showdown between the House and Senate. The legislature's been passing laws over the last several years, putting more restrictions on labor unions across the state and this year is no different. hundreds of thousands across the state are going to lose their rights, death by a thousand bureaucratic paper cuts should this legislation pass. Please vote no. And I stand in strong opposition of this bill. After one, more than 100 electricians, bus drivers, teachers, sanitation workers, and other public employees urged senators Monday to stop putting more restrictions on labor unions across the state. Dozens of them rallied before the Senate Fiscal Policy meeting concerned that these changes could do more harm. We do not need a piece of legislation like Senate Bill 1296 that is going to harm us even further than we already are and make it harder than it already is to continue doing the job. The committee made changes to Senate Bill 1296 while still building off public employee union requirements implemented a couple years ago. The changes require unions to have 20% of their members vote on ratification and recertification, and then 60% to pass. The bill also limits when they can take paid leave to advocate for union issues. Polk County teacher Laura Allgood says this bill could make life more difficult for unions and their members. I love teaching and I love my students and I want to continue to do this job and I don't want to do it any harder than it already is now. And I urge you, please vote no. It's important to have a safeguard in here. I think a simple majority is like, it's, it it feels common sense to me. Senator Jonathan Martin is carrying the bill. He says it's needed to make sure more people have the right to work. in certifying this bargaining group, you're requiring every other person out there who's in that group to keep their mouth shut. They don't have the ability to go and negotiate their own um, their own salary, their own benefits. The house has a similar bill ready for a vote, but it doesn't include the changes made in the Senate on Monday. Al says lawmakers should be focusing on several other issues instead. my students, the families, the things that I see because they can't make a living. I see we have out of control discipline. We have so many things going on in our school. We need to be focusing on that. Now if this does become law, there are likely to be legal challenges. A legislative staff analysis says that provisions in this bill could be unconstitutional. At the Florida State Capitol, I'm Cody Butler reporting.

Also, it currently supports only certain markets, so availability can be hit or miss. Still, for full-time gig drivers, Maestro can feel like having a digital co-pilot. If you want to maximize rides and reduce the chaos of app switching, it's worth considering. Just know you're paying for convenience, not magic.

answer: In today's video, I'll show you how to connect your AirPods to your Apple Watch. For the demonstration, I'll be connecting my AirPods Gen 4 and the Nord Buds 3 to the Apple Watch Series 10. You can follow these steps to connect your Apple Watch to any Bluetooth earbuds. The process is very simple. First, I'll show you how to connect the AirPods Gen 4. Open settings on your Apple Watch. Tap on Bluetooth and turn on the Bluetooth toggle button. Now, grab your AirPods and make sure that they are not connected to any device. You have to put them in pairing mode. To do that, open the lid of your AirPods, you'll see that the LED on the case has started to glow. Tap on it two times till it starts to flash white. I just have to select them and they are connected to my Apple Watch. If you're having any trouble connecting your AirPods or Bluetooth earbuds with your Apple Watch, then here are some things you can try to fix it. Make sure that both the Apple Watch and your AirPods are running the latest software versions. Software updates can often fix any bugs that might hamper connectivity. Next, ensure that you have enabled Bluetooth on your Apple Watch. Also, make sure that AirPods or Bluetooth earbuds are in pairing mode. Steps to enter pairing mode differ from earbud to earbud. So refer to the user manual of your earbuds for that. You can also try rebooting your Apple Watch. Rebooting will fix any glitch that might be hindering the pairing process. Finally, if nothing seems to work, then try resetting your AirPods. To reset the AirPods 4, you need to double tap three times on the status light till it flashes amber. For different earbuds, the steps to reset are different. And that's it for this one. Hello, I'm Sanya for TM News English. Tensions flared in Manchester City Centre today as far-right demonstrators clashed with counter-protesters, leading to multiple arrests and a major police operation. Let's see the report.
Hundreds of far-right demonstrators clashed with larger groups of counter-protesters in Manchester city centre during a tense standoff that led to multiple arrests. Supporters of Britain First gathered on Saturday for an anti-Islam march, chanting anti-immigration slogans beneath a city centre underpass as Union Jacks fluttered overhead. Some protesters appeared to be under the influence of alcohol as they criticized migrants and Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer. A counter-demonstration, organized by anti-fascist groups, drew a significantly larger crowd a few streets away. Protesters carried anti-racist placards and flags, including Palestinian flags, and accused Britain First of promoting racist and divisive views. As the two marches converged, tensions escalated. Protesters traded insults and police struggled to keep the groups apart. Some Britain First supporters reportedly prodded counter-protesters with flagpoles while others slipped through police lines. Officers described the operation as particularly challenging, with routes changing and additional events in the city stretching resources. Greater Manchester Police said nine men were arrested on suspicion of offences including assaulting an emergency worker, public order offences, breach of the peace and breaching a dispersal notice. A dispersal order was put in place across the city centre until 8 p.m., giving officers powers to remove individuals from the area. Assistant Chief Constable Rick Jackson said additional officers, including mounted and dog units, were deployed to support peaceful protest while minimizing disruption to the wider public.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Well, this G20 summit is unique for a few reasons. First of all, it's the first time in the 26-year history of G20s that leaders are meeting on this continent, the first time in Africa. It's also unique because it's the first G20 where the leaders of the three biggest economies are not present. No Russia, of course, no China, and the United States President Donald Trump, he's not here. He's boycotting this summit because he believes a genocide is being perpetrated against the white farmers of South Africa. He's wrong, that's a false claim, but that's uh that's Trump's belief. And yet, even though Trump is absent, he's really dominated the first few hours of the summit because of this peace plan that he wants to force on Ukraine. That peace plan was leaked yesterday, 28 points in it, and Trump has said that unless Zelensky, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accepts this peace plan by Thursday, the US may be looking at withdrawing military aid. For Zelensky, he says this is the most serious moment in Ukrainian history. Uh the peace plan would call for Ukraine to give up large chunks of the eastern part of its country to Russia. It would call on the Ukraine military to be weakened, and it would call on Ukraine to swear off uh joining NATO. Those are all non-starters for Ukraine. They're also non-starters for many of Ukraine's allies, Canada included. And so, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is stepping away from the summit activity to meet with European Council President Antonio Costa, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, French President Emmanuel Macron, and UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer. They'll all be stepping away to talk about how they can support Zelensky through this week ahead, what to do if in fact the US decides to pull military aid. Uh the Ukraine and the war uh war there has forced its way onto a summit which ostensibly was going to be about development, the Global South, uh new trade ties, etc. There will be that talk, but again, Ukraine has forced its way onto the agenda of this G20 summit. David Aken, Global News, Johannesburg.

answer: Spain held state-led memorials marking the one-year anniversary of the Valencia floods that killed 237 people, with a national ceremony in Valencia attended by King Felipe and Queen Letizia, regional officials, victims' relatives and large public demonstrations. At the state funeral, relatives, accompanied by the monarchs, laid a wreath in national colors and the names of victims were read aloud. King Felipe urged authorities to investigate the causes and circumstances of the tragedy to draw lessons and bolster emergency responses. Emotions ran high. A relative publicly blamed regional leader Carlos Mazón for failings that contributed to the loss of life, and some attendees shouted demands for his resignation as the ceremony closed. Outside official proceedings, tens of thousands joined torchlit processions and silent marches across Valencia and nearby towns. In a symbolic act, 229 emergency foil blankets, one for each person killed in the Valencia region, were placed in public squares to highlight the scale of the loss. Families and residents continued to press for accountability amid ongoing court inquiries into Mazón's conduct and whereabouts during the emergency, prompted by reports that he spent hours at a lunch when he was expected at an emergency meeting. Mazón denies wrongdoing and says he remained informed by phone but has declined to release details or the restaurant bill. The floods were produced by a DANA, Depresión Aislada en Niveles Altos, weather event that unleashed torrents of rain and sudden flash flooding, in some places delivering the equivalent of a year's precipitation within hours.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Welcome to Vacuum Wars where we're covering the latest news coming out of CES 2026. And Roborock has just introduced a product that might finally solve one of the biggest limitations in the robot vacuum industry, and it's called the Roborock Seros Rover. And according to the company, it features the world's first robot vacuum with stair climbing legs. At IFA in Berlin last year, we saw brands like Dreamy, Mova and Eufy try to tackle the stair climbing issue with separate climbing modules that carried the robot itself up and down the stairs. But those modules are pretty big and they can't actually vacuum the stairs themselves. The robots just get carried up and down the stairs. The new Seros Rover uses a legs with wheels architecture where each wheel is paired with a leg like mechanism. These can deploy independently to keep the robot's body level on uneven surfaces, slopes, and yes, stairs. Roborock says that this design allows it to raise and lower each wheel independently, execute agile turns and perform movements intended to imitate human mobility. They're using AI algorithms paired with motion sensors and 3D spatial information to make this happen, which is much more in line with what's happening in humanoid robotics lately, and it's pretty exciting to see. This would presumably completely solve the threshold climbing issue, but the biggest win here for the robot vacuum industry is that the Seros Rover doesn't just climb, it cleans every step as it goes. Also, it seems to be significantly smaller than the other prototype stair climbers that we've seen so far. There's also demo footage showing the robot executing small jumps to clear laser obstacles and maintaining its balance while testers throw tennis balls at it. I'm not sure what the application of either of these would be for robot vacuums, but it all suggests that this technology isn't just about climbing, it's about physically reacting to a dynamic environment in a way that we just haven't seen before. Roborock does emphasize that the Seros Rover is currently in development and the launch date is unconfirmed. There are still major questions that we at Vacuum Wars still would like to be answered, and I hope to have some of those answers at least in our full coverage of CES 2026 in a video coming out this Friday. We will also be putting out short form videos on TikTok and YouTube Shorts all this week during CES. So, stay tuned for our big CES coverage video this Friday and be sure to subscribe to Vacuum Wars here on YouTube or TikTok to keep up with all the latest information about CES 2026.

answer:
For weeks, Pixel 10A looked like one of the most predictable upgrades Google has ever done. Same display size, same cameras, same battery. But now a full spec sheet suggests at least five meaningful upgrades that weren't previously expected. And on top of that, 28 official-looking images just leaked, showing the entire design from every angle. Let's break it down.

First, the design. Google has already officially shown the design, and now these images also came out showing every side of the device. At first, the Pixel 10A looked very similar to Pixel 9A. Some are even calling it a Pixel 9B. But there's actually three upgrades to the design. First, the camera module is now rounder and flatter with almost no camera bump at all. One of the cleanest looks we have seen on a budget Pixel. Now, the spec sheet confirms Gorilla Glass 7i, replacing Gorilla Glass 3 from the Pixel 9A. That's a significant jump in scratch and drop resistance. And surprisingly, the phone is lighter than before. These changes suggest Google has refined the design rather than ruining it like other brands are doing. Similar situation can be seen on other specs. Google is bringing two big upgrades in terms of connectivity. First, the Pixel 10A is confirmed to upgrade from Bluetooth 5.3 to Bluetooth 6, meaning better security, improved efficiency, and boost data speed. Second, satellite emergency calling. That's a flagship-level feature, now trickling into Google's A-series. And finally, charging. We can also see a 45-watt charging speed. Compared to Pixel 9A, that's about 90-plus percent faster charging power. That's great because already Pixel 9A had one of the largest batteries in its class. Faster charging turns it into a serious endurance competitor. The specs list also confirmed the color namings: Obsidian, Folk, Lavender, and Berry. So, now, put it all together: stronger glass, lighter body, Bluetooth 6, satellite emergency support, and 45-watt charging. This spec suggests a refined device to Pixel 9A. Let me know, are you going for the Pixel 9A or the 10A? If you want to know what Apple has to offer with 17E, that's about to release as well. Here's my other video. I'll meet you there.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Hello everyone and welcome. A major political shock wave is shaking global diplomacy today. President Donald Trump has issued a direct ultimatum to Ukraine, and the deadline is just days away. Accept the peace plan or risk losing crucial US support is, Ukraine now standing at one of the most decisive moments in its history? Stay with me as we break down the full story. President Trump has presented a peace plan that appears surprisingly close to Russia's demands. The 28-point proposal calls for Ukraine to withdraw from the remaining parts of the Donbass region, reduce the size of its military, and abandon any intention of joining NATO. These are the same points Ukraine has repeatedly rejected in the past. On the battlefield, Ukraine is already under immense pressure. Russian drone strikes, constant bombardments, and difficult conditions on the eastern front. And now, pressure from the nation that has been its most important ally, the United States. President Zelensky has made it clear that Ukraine will not trade its dignity or freedom. But he also warned that if the United States steps back, the consequences for Ukraine could be severe. Zelensky has said, we need to find a balance to protect our freedom and also maintain our partnership with the US. But the Ukrainian public is strongly critical. Many believe this proposal would strengthen Russia, lift sanctions prematurely, and open the door for future conflicts by allowing Moscow to rebuild its military power. Meanwhile, the G20 summit is underway in South Africa. European leaders are present, France, Germany, the UK, all discussing how to respond to Trump's proposal. But the United States has boycotted the meeting. President Trump is not attending. So why isn't he there? Trump claims there is a genocide against white people in South Africa, a claim widely rejected by international organizations. He also criticized South Africa's land reforms. Some analysts say Trump simply opposes the multilateral framework that the G20 represents. The next few days will be critical. If Ukraine rejects Trump's plan, it risks losing essential US support. If it accepts the plan, it may have to surrender territory and compromise its long-term security. Either choice could reshape the course of this war and Ukraine's future. So what do you think? Will Ukraine stand firm or will international pressure force a compromise? Share your thoughts in the comments below. And if you found this video insightful, make sure you like, share, and subscribe so you never miss an update. Thanks for watching. See you in the next video.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer:
We are going back to the turning point in human history, to the Arabian Peninsula around 1400 years ago. In this 11-part series, you will explore the life of Prophet Muhammad alaihi salatu wassalam in ways you have never heard before. Sometimes we will find ourselves in the early days of revelation, in the secret gatherings of Muslims at Darul Arqam. Other times, the excitement will rise as we witness Omar radiyallahu anhu fearlessly walking towards the idol worshipers of Mecca. Whoever kills Muhammad, I will reward him with 100 red and black camels. This is what happens to those who obey Muhammad. Take this as a warning. There will be times when we are sad and moved to tears, times when we feel afraid, and times when we cannot help but smile. But most of the time, our hearts will be filled with peace. From the story of a prophet who showed us how to find a way out even in the most hopeless situations, we will learn how to overcome the dead ends of our own lives. We won't just look at the events and move on. We will also try to understand the deep meanings behind them. This journey will lead you to a whole new path and rediscover who you truly are. This is the story of the most beloved to Allah. A man who would sacrifice his entire life for his ummah, who would be betrayed and slandered by hypocrites over and over again. There would be times when he would be left hungry for months, and times when he would lose his loved ones and bury them with his own hands. He would always call people to light, to guidance, but in return, he would be pelted with stones. I have never seen anyone bring this much evil and wickedness to his own family like you have. He would face countless assassination attempts, but not even for a moment would he give up on his mission. And in the end, Allah would fulfill his promise to his loyal servant. We are now embarking on an unprecedented 23-year journey. You will witness the story of an extraordinary man who started this cause alone, stood up to the entire world, and today has over 2 billion followers behind him. If you're ready, let's begin.
This Ramadan on the Towards Eternity YouTube channel. Subscribe, turn on notifications, and stay tuned, so you don't miss this series.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: This is the new Watchtowers Network's Sentinel camera station, standing tall at Mount Ike in the Riverina Highlands. A cornerstone of an integrated bushfire detection and monitoring network operated by the New South Wales Rural Fire Service, New South Wales Parks and Wildlife, and a consortium of forestry organizations that protects the southern regions of the state. With AI powered detection and real-time alerts, the Mount Ike site integrates with an expansive network across the snowy valleys to provide unmatched visibility, spotting fires up to 70 km away, day or night. By providing early warnings to fire services and communities through the new Central Watch platform, this new capability strengthens the snowy Valley's resilience to bushfire threats. Co-funded by the Department of Primary Industries and the Softwoods working group and enabled by a partnership with the New South Wales Telco Authority and police to co-locate on their tower, this site is a model of collaboration. Together, we're safeguarding lives, properties, and the landscapes of the Snowy Valley community, building resilience against bushfires with state-of-the-art technology. Join us in building a safer Riverina Highlands. Visit Watchtower's website to explore Central Watch and discover how we're building a safer future together.

answer: Have you ever wondered what secrets lie deep beneath the ocean's surface? Close your eyes and dive in with me. Splash. You're now swimming in the deep blue sea. But wait, what's that? A shadow is moving fast. It's a dolphin and it wants to race. You try to keep up, but dolphins are the ocean's speed champions. They click, whistle, and laugh, as if they're cheering you on. As you dive deeper, the water gets darker. Something glides past. It's a sea turtle, slow and graceful. She's been swimming for 50 years, and now she's returning to the beach where she was born. Just to lay her eggs. She nods at you, like she remembers something from long ago. Suddenly, the water changes color. Not because of the sun, but because of an octopus. It squirts ink and disappears into the rocks. Wait, did it just change color to match the coral? And did it just open a jar with its arms? That's one smart sea creature. You keep swimming, and then you feel it. A strange, soft glow all around you. Jellyfish. Dozens of them, glowing in the dark like underwater stars. They float gently, silently. Beautiful, but mysterious. Then just when you think nothing could be more magical, you hear a low, distant sound, like a drum beat. Boom. Boom. Boom. A giant shape approaches. It's the blue whale, the biggest animal to ever live. Bigger than any dinosaur. And its heart? The size of a car. You float beside it, feeling very small, but not afraid. Because here in the ocean, everything has its place. And now, you're a part of it too. The ocean is waiting for you. Full of stories, full of wonders. Will you return?

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Google Beam projects people as life-sized 3D holograms directly into your space, fixing the fundamental problems that make video calls feel disconnected and awkward. I'll show you how this technology works and why it's a genuine leap forward for remote communication. Hey everyone, here at Bitbias.ai, we do the research so you don't have to. Today, we're looking at Google Beam, previously known as Project Starline. I got hands-on with this holographic meeting technology, and I'll show you exactly how it works and the real impact it's having on professional communication. Video calls have been broken since day one. You stare at tiny squares, struggle with eye contact, and lose all the natural human connection that makes in-person meetings effective. Google Beam fixes this completely by making remote people appear as life-sized, three-dimensional holograms in your space. This isn't science fiction anymore. The technology uses multiple cameras to capture every angle and creates a real-time 3D presence that moves and responds naturally. The difference in meeting quality is dramatic. When someone appears as a hologram sitting across from you, your brain processes them as actually being there. Eye contact works properly, body language becomes meaningful again. The awkwardness of video calls disappears because the technology gets out of the way of human connection. I experienced this firsthand during a demonstration, and the psychological impact was immediate. Instead of managing the technology, I was focused entirely on the conversation. The person felt present in a way that traditional video calls never achieve. Early enterprise testing shows promising results. Companies using Beam report 60% better meeting engagement and significantly improved decision-making in remote collaborations. One sales team I spoke with closed three major deals in their first week using the technology, crediting the enhanced personal connection. Remote consultations and client meetings are becoming noticeably more effective when participants feel physically present. Google is partnering with major companies like HP and Zoom to integrate this into workplace environments. The technology requires specialized hardware, so it'll likely appear in conference rooms and professional settings first before becoming widely accessible. The timeline for broader availability is later this year for enterprise customers with consumer applications following. This represents the future of remote communication and the organizations that adopt it early will have a significant advantage in building relationships and conducting business remotely. Remote work and global collaboration just evolved beyond recognition and the companies using this technology will set new standards for what professional communication looks like. So there you have it. Google Beam is fundamentally changing how remote meetings work. What type of meetings do you think would benefit most from this technology? Client presentations, team collaborations, or something else entirely? Let me know in the comments, and if you want to stay updated on when this becomes available, hit that subscribe button.

The two-time Olympic champion and holder of two world records will chase not only victory, but also the coveted World Marathon Major Six-Star medal, completing wins in all six major marathons. Kipchoge faces a world-class lineup that includes defending champion Abdi Nageeye, former winner Albert Korir, and Ethiopian legend Kenenisa Bekele, who returns after setting a world masters record in London earlier this year. Benson Kipruto, the 2024 Olympic bronze medalist, and Alexander Mutiso, this year's London Marathon champion, both bring blistering personal bests under 2 hours and 4 minutes. Tanzania's Alphonce Simbu, the reigning world champion, adds even more depth to this historic field. For the USA, Ababiya Simbasa leads the charge after clocking 2 hours, 6 minutes, 53 seconds in Valencia. On the women's side, Olympic marathon champion Sifan Hassan headlines a dream lineup. The Dutch superstar, fresh from a golden performance in Paris 2024, seeks a third World Marathon Major win after victories in London and Chicago. She will be tested by a trio of Kenyan champions, Sharon Lokedi, Hellen Obiri, and Sheila Chepkirui. Ethiopia's Gotytom Gebresilase, the 2022 world champion and veteran Vivian Cheruiyot, the Rio Olympic gold medalist, add star power and experience. The American women bring serious firepower too. National record holder Emily Sisson makes her New York debut, while Olympic medalist Molly Seidel and World Championship standout Susanna Sullivan look to challenge for a podium. For Olympic glory to personal redemption, the 2025 New York City Marathon promises drama, rivalry, and history in the making.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: How do product reviews compare to official appliance ratings? Have you ever wondered how product reviews stack up against official appliance ratings? Let's break it down so you can make informed choices when shopping for home appliances. Official appliance ratings come from independent organizations or testing labs. These ratings are created using standardized methods to evaluate appliances. They focus on measurable factors like performance, energy efficiency, durability, and reliability. The testing is consistent across all products in a category, which allows for straightforward comparisons. You can expect detailed data from these ratings, and they are conducted without any influence from manufacturers. This means you receive unbiased and objective information. On the other hand, product reviews, especially those from users or customers, reflected individual experiences with appliances in real-world settings. These reviews can give you a glimpse into everyday use, customer satisfaction, and practical issues like ease of use and noise levels. However, the quality of user reviews can vary widely. Some may be subjective or influenced by personal expectations. You might find reviews that are overly positive or negative, which may not representing the typical experience. Professional review sites and consumer organizations often combine both methods. They conduct their own tests while also considering user feedback. By purchasing appliances as regular customers, they avoid any bias from manufacturers. This results in ratings that are both data-driven and reflective of actual usage. When it comes to home appliances, relying on official ratings helps you understand the technical performance and reliability of a product. Meanwhile, product reviews can highlight real-life advantages or issues that might not show up in lab tests. For instance, you might learn about customer service quality or how well an appliance fits into a typical household environment. So, how can you use this information when choosing home appliances? Start by looking at official ratings to narrow down your options based on objective performance and efficiency. After that, check out product reviews to learn about user experiences, common problems, and satisfaction levels. By combining both sources, you can make a more informed purchase decision that balances technical quality with everyday usability.
